sentences.zh: 郊祀 郊祀配位 郊祀儀注 祈穀 大雩 大饗 令節 拜天

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifices; matched seats at suburban sacrifices; regulations for suburban sacrifices; prayer for grain; great rain prayer; great feasts; statutory festivals; worshipping Heaven
translations.idiomatic: Suburban Sacrifices; Matched Seats at Suburban Sacrifices; Regulations for Suburban Sacrifices; Prayer for Grain; Great Rain Prayer; Great Feasts; Statutory Festivals; Worshipping Heaven

sentences.zh: ○郊祀之制

translations.literal: ○ Regulations on suburban sacrifices
translations.idiomatic: Regulations on Suburban Sacrifices

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，中書省臣李善長等奉敕撰進《郊祀議》，略言：

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, Li Shanchang and other ministers of the Secretariat, by imperial command, drafted and submitted the 《Discourse on Suburban Sacrifices》, which stated in summary:
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1, Li Shanchang and other Secretariat ministers were commanded to draft and submit the 《Discourse on Suburban Sacrifices》, which stated in summary:

sentences.zh: 王者事天明，事地察，故冬至報天，夏至報地，所以順陰陽之義也。

translations.literal: The king serves Heaven with clarity and serves Earth with discernment; therefore at the winter solstice he reports to Heaven and at the summer solstice reports to Earth—this accords with the principle of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler serves Heaven with clarity and Earth with discernment; at the winter solstice he reports to Heaven and at the summer solstice to Earth—thus honoring the balance of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 祭天於南郊之圜丘，祭地於北郊之方澤，所以順陰陽之位也。

translations.literal: Heaven is sacrificed to at the Circular Mound in the southern suburb, and Earth at the Square Mound in the northern suburb—this accords with the positions of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is worshipped at the Circular Mound in the southern suburb and Earth at the Square Mound in the northern suburb—thus matching the stations of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·大司樂》：「冬日至，禮天神，夏日至，禮地祇。

translations.literal: The 《Rites of Zhou · Grand Music Master》 says: "At the winter solstice, honor the spirit of Heaven; at the summer solstice, honor the spirit of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou · Grand Music Master》 states: "At the winter solstice, honor the spirit of Heaven; at the summer solstice, honor the spirit of Earth.

sentences.zh: 」《禮》曰：「享帝於郊，祀社於國。

translations.literal: " The 《Rites》 says: "Honor the Emperor in the suburbs; sacrifice to the god of soil in the state.
translations.idiomatic: " The 《Rites》 says: "Honor the Emperor in the suburbs; sacrifice to the god of soil within the realm.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「郊所以明天道，社所以明地道。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The suburbs illuminate the Way of Heaven; the altars of soil illuminate the Way of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "The suburban rites reveal the Way of Heaven; the altars of soil reveal the Way of Earth.

sentences.zh: 」《書》曰：「敢昭告於皇天后土。

translations.literal: " The 《Documents》 says: "I venture to make clear announcement to August Heaven and Sovereign Earth.
translations.idiomatic: " The 《Documents》 says: "I venture to proclaim clearly to August Heaven and Sovereign Earth.

sentences.zh: 」按古者或曰地祇，或曰后土，或曰社，皆祭地，則皆對天而言也。

translations.literal: " According to antiquity, [Earth] was called either the Spirit of Earth, or Queen Earth, or the God of Soil—all are sacrifices to Earth, and all are spoken of in relation to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " In antiquity Earth was called the Spirit of Earth, Queen Earth, or the God of Soil—all are sacrifices to Earth, and all are defined in relation to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 此三代之正禮，而釋經之正說。

translations.literal: This was the orthodox ritual of the Three Dynasties and the orthodox interpretation in explicating the classics.
translations.idiomatic: This was the orthodox ritual of the Three Dynasties and the authoritative reading in exegesis of the classics.

sentences.zh: 自秦立四畤，以祀白、青、黃、赤四帝。

translations.literal: From the Qin, four shrines were established to sacrifice to the White, Green, Yellow, and Red Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin onward four shrines were established to sacrifice to the White, Green, Yellow, and Red Emperors.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖復增北畤，兼祀黑帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han further added the northern shrine, also sacrificing to the Black Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han added a northern shrine and also sacrificed to the Black Emperor.

sentences.zh: 至武帝有雍五畤，及渭陽五帝、甘泉太乙之祠，而昊天上帝之祭則未嘗舉行，魏、晉以後，宗鄭玄者，以為天有六名，歲凡九祭。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wu there were the five shrines of Yong, the sacrifices to the Five Emperors at Weiyang, and the Grand Unity shrine at Ganquan, yet sacrifice to August Heaven, Sovereign on High was never performed. After Wei and Jin, those who followed Zheng Xuan held that Heaven had six names and that in a year there were nine sacrifices in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu came the five shrines of Yong, the Five Emperors at Weiyang, and the Grand Unity shrine at Ganquan—yet sacrifice to August Heaven, Sovereign on High was never performed. After Wei and Jin, followers of Zheng Xuan held that Heaven had six names and that the year required nine sacrifices in all.

sentences.zh: 宗王肅者，以為天體惟一，安得有六？

translations.literal: Those who followed Wang Su held that the body of Heaven is singular—how could there be six?
translations.idiomatic: Followers of Wang Su argued that Heaven's body is one—how could there be six?

sentences.zh: 一歲二祭，安得有九？

translations.literal: Two sacrifices in one year—how could there be nine?
translations.idiomatic: Two sacrifices in a year—how could there be nine?

sentences.zh: 雖因革不同，大抵多參二家之說。

translations.literal: Although reforms differed, for the most part both schools' views were combined.
translations.idiomatic: Though reforms differed, for the most part both schools' views were blended together.

sentences.zh: 自漢武用祠官寬舒議，立后土祠於汾陰脽上，禮如祀天。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu of Han, following the proposal of the sacrificial officer Kuanshu, a shrine to Queen Earth was established on the mound at Fenyin—its ritual was like sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wu of Han, adopting the proposal of the sacrificial officer Kuanshu, a shrine to Queen Earth was built on the mound at Fenyin, with rites like those for Heaven.

sentences.zh: 而後世因於北郊之外，仍祠后土。

translations.literal: Later generations therefore continued to sacrifice to Queen Earth beyond the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages continued to sacrifice to Queen Earth beyond the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 又鄭玄惑於緯書，謂夏至於方丘之上祭昆侖之祇，七月於泰折之壇祭神州之祇，析而為二。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan was moreover misled by apocryphal texts, holding that at the summer solstice the Spirit of Kunlun was sacrificed to atop the Square Mound, and in the seventh month the Spirit of the Divine Land on the altar of Taizhe—splitting this into two.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan was further misled by apocryphal texts, holding that at the summer solstice the Spirit of Kunlun was sacrificed atop the Square Mound and in the seventh month the Spirit of the Divine Land on the Taizhe altar—thus splitting Earth into two rites.

sentences.zh: 後世又因之一歲二祭。

translations.literal: Later generations again followed this, with two sacrifices in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages again followed this practice of two sacrifices in one year.

sentences.zh: 元始間，王莽奏罷甘泉泰畤，復長安南北郊。

translations.literal: During the Yuanshi reign, Wang Mang memorialized to abolish the Tai altar at Ganquan and restore the southern and northern suburbs of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanshi era Wang Mang memorialized to abolish the Tai altar at Ganquan and restore Chang'an's southern and northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 以正月上辛若丁，天子親合祀天地於南郊。

translations.literal: On the first xin or ding day of the first month, the Son of Heaven would in person perform the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xin or ding day of the first month the Son of Heaven would personally perform the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 由漢歷唐，千餘年間，皆因之合祭。

translations.literal: From Han through Tang, for more than a thousand years, all followed this joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Tang, for more than a thousand years, all followed this joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其親祀北郊者，惟魏文帝、周武帝、隋高祖、唐玄宗四帝而已。

translations.literal: Those who in person sacrificed at the northern suburb were only four emperors: Wen of Wei, Wu of Zhou, Gaozu of Sui, and Xuanzong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Only four emperors personally sacrificed at the northern suburb: Emperor Wen of Wei, Emperor Wu of Zhou, Emperor Gaozu of Sui, and Emperor Xuanzong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 宋元豐中，議罷合祭。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era of Song, there was discussion of abolishing the joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng era of Song there was debate over abolishing the joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 紹聖、政和間，或分或合。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng and Zhenghe periods, [rites] were sometimes separate and sometimes combined.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaosheng and Zhenghe periods the rites were sometimes separate and sometimes combined.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡以後，惟用合祭之禮。

translations.literal: After Gaozong's flight south of the Yangtze, only the ritual of joint sacrifice was used.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong crossed south of the Yangtze, only the joint sacrifice was used.

sentences.zh: 元成宗始合祭天地五方帝，已而立南郊，專祀天。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong of Yuan at first jointly sacrificed to Heaven, Earth, and the Five Directional Emperors; afterward he established the southern suburb and sacrificed to Heaven alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzong of Yuan at first jointly sacrificed to Heaven, Earth, and the Five Directional Emperors; later he established the southern suburb and sacrificed to Heaven alone.

sentences.zh: 泰定中，又合祭。

translations.literal: In the Taiding era, joint sacrifice was resumed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiding era joint sacrifice was resumed.

sentences.zh: 文宗至順以後，惟祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: After Wenzong's Zhishun reign, only August Heaven, Sovereign on High was sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong's Zhishun reign only August Heaven, Sovereign on High was worshipped.

sentences.zh: 今當遵古制，分祭天地於南北郊。

translations.literal: Now the ancient system should be followed, with Heaven and Earth separately sacrificed to at the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ancient system should be followed, with Heaven and Earth sacrificed separately at the southern and northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 冬至則祀昊天上帝於圜丘，以大明、夜明、星辰、太歲從祀。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice August Heaven, Sovereign on High shall be sacrificed to at the Circular Mound, with the great luminaries day and night, the stars, and the Grand Year-star as attendant sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice August Heaven, Sovereign on High shall be worshipped at the Circular Mound, with the great luminaries of day and night, the stars, and the Grand Year-star as attendant sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 夏至則祀皇地祇於方丘，以五嶽、五鎮、四海、四瀆從祀。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth shall be sacrificed to at the Square Mound, with the Five Sacred Peaks, Five Guardian Mountains, Four Seas, and Four Great Rivers as attendant sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth shall be worshipped at the Square Mound, with the Five Sacred Peaks, Five Guardian Mountains, Four Seas, and Four Great Rivers as attendant sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太祖如其議行之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor followed this proposal and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor adopted this proposal and put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 建圜丘於鐘山之陽，方丘於鐘山之陰。

translations.literal: A Circular Mound was built on the sunny slope of Bell Mountain and a Square Mound on its shaded slope.
translations.idiomatic: A Circular Mound was built on the sunny slope of Bell Mountain and a Square Mound on its shaded slope.

sentences.zh: 三年，增祀風雲雷雨於圜丘，天下山川之神於方丘。

translations.literal: In the third year, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain were added to sacrifices at the Circular Mound, and the spirits of mountains and rivers throughout the realm to sacrifices at the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year wind, clouds, thunder, and rain were added to the Circular Mound sacrifices, and the spirits of mountains and rivers throughout the realm to the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 七年，增設天下神祇壇於南北郊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, altars to the spirits of the realm were additionally established at the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year altars to the spirits of the realm were added at the southern and northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 九年，定郊社之禮，雖有三年喪，不廢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the ritual of suburban and soil-altar sacrifices was fixed, so that even during the three-year mourning period they were not discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the suburban and soil-altar rites were fixed so that even during the three-year mourning period they were not suspended.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，太祖感齋居陰雨，覽京房災異之說，謂分祭天地，情有未安，命作大祀殿於南郊。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year, during fasting the Founding Emperor, troubled by continuous rain, read Jing Fang's discourse on portents and calamities and felt uneasy about separate sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; he ordered the Grand Sacrifice Hall built at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the tenth year, while fasting the Founding Emperor was troubled by unending rain, read Jing Fang's discourse on portents and calamities, felt uneasy about separate sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, and ordered the Grand Sacrifice Hall built at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬至，以殿工未成，乃合祀於奉天殿，而親制祝文，意謂人君事天地猶父母，不宜異處。

translations.literal: That winter solstice, because construction on the hall was not yet complete, the joint sacrifice was performed in the Hall of Receiving Heaven, and he personally composed the prayer text, taking the view that the ruler's service to Heaven and Earth is like [a child's service] to father and mother and that they should not be separated.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice, because the hall was not yet finished, the joint sacrifice was held in the Hall of Receiving Heaven; the Founding Emperor personally composed the prayer, holding that the ruler serves Heaven and Earth as a child serves parents and that they should not be worshipped apart.

sentences.zh: 遂定每歲合祀於孟春，為永制。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was fixed that each year the joint sacrifice would be held in the first month of spring as a permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was fixed that each year the joint sacrifice would be held in the first month of spring as a permanent institution.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，始合祀於大祀殿，太祖親作《大祀文》並歌九章。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, the joint sacrifice was first performed in the Grand Sacrifice Hall; the Founding Emperor personally composed the 《Grand Sacrifice Text》 and nine hymn chapters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year the joint sacrifice was first performed in the Grand Sacrifice Hall; the Founding Emperor personally composed the 《Grand Sacrifice Text》 and nine hymn chapters.

sentences.zh: 永樂十八年，京都大祀殿成，規制如南京。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yongle, the capital's Grand Sacrifice Hall was completed, its regulations like those of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 18 the capital's Grand Sacrifice Hall was completed, on the same plan as Nanjing's.

sentences.zh: 南京舊郊壇，國有大事，則遣官告祭。

translations.literal: The old suburban altars of Nanjing—for great affairs of state, officials were dispatched to announce and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing's old suburban altars, when the state faced great affairs, officials were dispatched to announce and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，世宗既定《明倫大典》，益覃思製作之事，郊廟百神，咸欲斟酌古法，釐正舊章。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, after the Emperor had settled the 《Great Compendium of Human Relations》, he pondered more deeply matters of institutional creation; for suburban altars and the spirits of the hundred sacrifices, he wished to weigh ancient methods and rectify old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9, after the Jiajing Emperor had settled the 《Great Compendium of Human Relations》, he turned his mind more deeply to institutional creation; for suburban altars and the hundred spirits he wished to weigh ancient methods and rectify old regulations.

sentences.zh: 乃問大學士張璁：「《書》稱燔柴祭天，又曰『類於上帝』，《孝經》曰：『郊祀后稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝』，以形體主宰之異言也。

translations.literal: He then asked Grand Secretary Zhang Cong: "The 《Documents》 speaks of burning firewood to sacrifice to Heaven, and also says 'to categorize [and sacrifice] to the Sovereign on High.' The 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: 'In the suburbs sacrifice to Hou Ji to match Heaven; in the ancestral temple honor King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign on High'—these speak of the difference between [Heaven as] bodily form and [as] ruling lord.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Grand Secretary Zhang Cong: "The 《Documents》 speaks of burning firewood to sacrifice to Heaven and also says 'to categorize [and sacrifice] to the Sovereign on High.' The 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: 'In the suburbs sacrifice to Hou Ji to match Heaven; in the ancestral temple honor King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign on High'—these distinguish Heaven as bodily form from Heaven as ruling lord.

sentences.zh: 硃子謂，祭之於壇謂之天，祭之屋下謂之帝。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi said that sacrifice on an altar is called Heaven and sacrifice under a roof is called the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said that sacrifice on an altar is called Heaven and sacrifice under a roof is called the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今大祀有殿，是屋下之祭帝耳，未見有祭天之禮也。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Sacrifice has a hall—this is sacrifice to the Emperor under a roof, and no ritual of sacrificing to Heaven is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Grand Sacrifice has a hall—that is sacrifice to the Emperor under a roof; no rite of sacrificing to Heaven is in evidence.

sentences.zh: 況上帝皇地祇合祭一處，亦非專祭上帝。

translations.literal: Moreover August Heaven, Sovereign on High and the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth are sacrificed to in one place—this too is not exclusive sacrifice to August Heaven, Sovereign on High.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover August Heaven, Sovereign on High and the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth are worshipped in one place—this is not exclusive worship of August Heaven, Sovereign on High.

sentences.zh: 」璁言：「國初遵古禮，分祭天地，後又合祀。

translations.literal: Cong replied: "At the founding of the realm the ancient ritual was followed, with separate sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; afterward joint sacrifice was resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied: "At the founding of the realm the ancient rites were followed, with Heaven and Earth sacrificed separately; later joint sacrifice was resumed.

sentences.zh: 說者謂大祀殿下壇上屋，屋即明堂，壇即圜丘，列聖相承，亦孔子從周之意。

translations.literal: Expositors say that beneath the Grand Sacrifice Hall is an altar and above it a roof—the roof is the Bright Hall and the altar is the Circular Mound; successive sage emperors inherited this, which is also the meaning of Confucius's following Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors say that beneath the Grand Sacrifice Hall is an altar and above it a roof—the roof is the Bright Hall and the altar the Circular Mound; successive sage emperors inherited this, in the spirit of Confucius's following Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」帝復諭璁：「二至分祀，萬代不易之禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor again instructed Cong: "Separate sacrifice at the two solstices is ritual that must never change through the ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again instructed Cong: "Separate sacrifice at the two solstices is ritual that must never change for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 今大祀殿擬周明堂或近矣，以為即圜丘，實無謂也。

translations.literal: Now to take the Grand Sacrifice Hall as approximating the Zhou Bright Hall may come close, but to treat it as the Circular Mound is truly meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: To liken the Grand Sacrifice Hall to the Zhou Bright Hall may come close, but to treat it as the Circular Mound is truly absurd.

sentences.zh: 」璁乃備述《周禮》及宋陳襄、蘇軾、劉安世、程頤所議分合異同以對。

translations.literal: Cong then set forth in full the discussions of separate and joint sacrifice in the 《Rites of Zhou》 and among the Song scholars Chen Xiang, Su Shi, Liu Anshi, and Cheng Yi to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Cong then set forth in full the arguments on separate and joint sacrifice in the 《Rites of Zhou》 and among the Song scholars Chen Xiang, Su Shi, Liu Anshi, and Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 且言祖制已定，無敢輕議。

translations.literal: He also said that the ancestral institution was already settled and none dared lightly debate it.
translations.idiomatic: He added that the ancestral institution was already settled and none dared debate it lightly.

sentences.zh: 帝銳欲定郊制，卜之奉先殿太祖前，不吉。

translations.literal: The Emperor, keen to fix the suburban ritual system, divined before the Founding Emperor in the Hall of the First Ancestors—with an inauspicious result.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, keen to fix the suburban ritual system, divined before the Founding Emperor in the Hall of the First Ancestors—with an inauspicious result.

sentences.zh: 乃問大學士翟鑾，鑾具述因革以對。

translations.literal: He then asked Grand Secretary Zhai Luan; Luan fully set forth the reforms and changes in answer.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Grand Secretary Zhai Luan, who fully set forth the history of reforms and changes.

sentences.zh: 復問禮部尚書李時，時請少需日月，博選儒臣，議復古制。

translations.literal: He again asked Minister of Rites Li Shi; Shi requested a few months' delay to select broadly among Confucian officials and discuss restoring the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked Minister of Rites Li Shi, who requested a few months' delay to select broadly among Confucian officials and discuss restoring the ancient system.

sentences.zh: 帝復卜之太祖，不吉，議且寢。

translations.literal: The Emperor again divined before the Founding Emperor—with an inauspicious result, and the discussion was suspended for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again divined before the Founding Emperor—with an inauspicious result, and the discussion was suspended for the time being.

sentences.zh: 會給事中夏言請舉親蠶禮。

translations.literal: At this time Supervising Secretary Xia Yan requested the performance of the personal silkworm-rearing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Supervising Secretary Xia Yan requested that the personal silkworm-rearing ritual be performed.

sentences.zh: 帝以古者天子親耕南郊，皇后親蠶北郊，適與所議郊祀相表裏，因令璁諭言陳郊議。

translations.literal: The Emperor noted that in antiquity the Son of Heaven personally ploughed in the southern suburb and the empress personally raised silkworms in the northern suburb—this precisely complemented the discussion of suburban sacrifice—and he therefore had Cong instruct Yan to present his views on suburban ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor noted that in antiquity the Son of Heaven personally ploughed in the southern suburb and the empress personally raised silkworms in the northern suburb—this paired naturally with the debate on suburban sacrifice—and he had Cong instruct Yan to present his views on suburban ritual.

sentences.zh: 言乃上疏言：「國家合祀天地，及太祖、太宗之並配，諸壇之從祀，舉行不於長至而於孟春，俱不應古典。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon submitted a memorial stating: "The state's joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the joint accompaniment of the Founding and Taizong Emperors, and the attendant sacrifices at the various altars, held not at the winter solstice but in the first month of spring—all fail to accord with classical antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a memorial stating: "The state's joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the joint accompaniment of the Founding and Taizong Emperors, and the attendant sacrifices at the various altars, held not at the winter solstice but in the first month of spring—all fail to accord with classical antiquity.

sentences.zh: 宜令羣臣博考《詩》、《書》、《禮經》所載郊祀之文，及漢、宋諸儒匡衡、劉安世、硃熹等之定論，以及太祖國初分祀之舊制，陛下稱制而裁定之。

translations.literal: Your ministers should be commanded to study broadly the texts on suburban sacrifice in the 《Odes》, 《Documents》, and ritual classics, the settled opinions of Han and Song Confucians such as Kuang Heng, Liu Anshi, and Zhu Xi, and the founding separate-sacrifice system of the Founding Emperor—whereupon Your Majesty may decide by your own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers should be commanded to study broadly the texts on suburban sacrifice in the 《Odes》, 《Documents》, and ritual classics, the settled opinions of Han and Song scholars such as Kuang Heng, Liu Anshi, and Zhu Xi, and the Founding Emperor's original separate-sacrifice system at the founding of the realm—whereupon Your Majesty may decide by your own authority.

sentences.zh: 此中興大業也。

translations.literal: This is a great enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: This would be a great enterprise of restoration.

sentences.zh: 」禮科給事中王汝梅等詆言說非是，帝切責之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Rumei of the Rites Section and others attacked Yan's views as wrong; the Emperor sharply rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rumei of the Rites Section and other supervising secretaries attacked Yan's views as wrong; the Emperor sharply rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 乃敕禮部令羣臣各陳所見。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to have all officials state their views.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Rites to have all officials state their views.

sentences.zh: 且言：「汝梅等舉《召誥》中郊用二牛，謂明言合祭天地。

translations.literal: And he said: "Rumei and others cite the two oxen used in the suburban sacrifice in the 《Announcement of Duke Shao》, taking this as clear evidence of joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: And he said: "Rumei and others cite the two oxen used in the suburban sacrifice in the 《Announcement of Duke Shao》, taking this as clear proof of joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 夫用二牛者，一帝一配位，非天地各一牛也。

translations.literal: Where two oxen are used, one is for the Emperor and one for the matched seat—it is not one ox each for Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Where two oxen are used, one is for the Emperor and one for the matched seat—it is not one ox each for Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 又或謂天地合祀，乃人子事父母之道，擬之夫婦同牢。

translations.literal: Others say joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth follows the way of a child serving father and mother, likening it to husband and wife sharing one funeral meal.
translations.idiomatic: Others say joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth follows the way of a child serving parents, likening it to husband and wife sharing one wedding meal.

sentences.zh: 此等言論，褻慢已甚。

translations.literal: Such discourse is grossly irreverent.
translations.idiomatic: Such talk is grossly irreverent.

sentences.zh: 又或謂郊為祀天，社稷為祭地。

translations.literal: Others say the suburb is sacrifice to Heaven and the altars of soil sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Others say the suburban rite worships Heaven and the altars of soil worship Earth.

sentences.zh: 古無北郊，夫社乃祭五土之祇，猶言五方帝耳，非皇地祇也。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was no northern suburb; the god of soil sacrifices to the spirit of the five soils—it is like speaking of the Five Directional Emperors, not the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there was no northern suburb; the god of soil sacrifices to the spirit of the five soils—it is like the Five Directional Emperors, not the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth.

sentences.zh: 社之名不同，自天子以下，皆得隨所在而祭之。

translations.literal: The name of the god of soil differs; from the Son of Heaven downward, all may sacrifice according to where they are.
translations.idiomatic: The name of the god of soil differs; from the Son of Heaven downward, all may sacrifice according to where they dwell.

sentences.zh: 故《禮》有『親地』之說，非謂祭社即方澤祭地也。

translations.literal: Therefore the 《Rites》 has the doctrine of 'personal sacrifice to Earth'—this does not mean that sacrificing to the god of soil is the Square Mound sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the 《Rites》 speaks of 'personal sacrifice to Earth'—this does not mean that sacrificing to the god of soil is the Square Mound sacrifice to Earth.

sentences.zh: 」璁因錄上《郊祀考議》一冊。

translations.literal: Cong thereupon recorded and submitted a volume of 《Studies on Suburban Sacrifice》.
translations.idiomatic: Cong thereupon recorded and submitted a volume of 《Studies on Suburban Sacrifice》.

sentences.zh: 時詹事霍韜深非郊議，且言分祀之說，惟見《周禮》，莽賊偽書，不足引據，於是言復上疏言：

translations.literal: At this time Grand Mentor Huo Tao strongly opposed the suburban discussion and held that the doctrine of separate sacrifice is found only in the 《Rites of Zhou》, a forged book of the rebel Wang Mang, insufficient for citation—whereupon Yan again submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: At this time Grand Mentor Huo Tao strongly opposed the suburban debate and held that the doctrine of separate sacrifice appears only in the 《Rites of Zhou》, a forged book of the rebel Wang Mang, insufficient for citation—whereupon Yan again submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 《周禮》一書，於祭祀為詳。

translations.literal: The book 《Rites of Zhou》 is detailed on sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou》 is detailed on sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《大宗伯》以祀天神，則有禋祀、實柴、槱燎之禮，以祀地祇，則有血祭、薶沈、趯辜之禮。

translations.literal: The 《Chief Sacrifices Officer》 for sacrificing to the spirit of Heaven has the rituals of smoke-offering, solid firewood, and bundle-burning; for sacrificing to the spirit of Earth it has blood sacrifice, burial immersion, and dismembered offering.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Chief Sacrifices Officer》 for worshipping the spirit of Heaven prescribes smoke-offering, solid firewood, and bundle-burning; for worshipping the spirit of Earth it prescribes blood sacrifice, burial immersion, and dismembered offering.

sentences.zh: 《大司樂》冬至日，地上圜丘之制，則曰禮天神，夏至日，澤中方丘之制，則曰禮地祇。

translations.literal: The 《Grand Music Master》 on the winter solstice day has the regulation of the Circular Mound above ground, saying 'honor the spirit of Heaven'; on the summer solstice day has the regulation of the Square Mound in the marsh, saying 'honor the spirit of Earth.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Grand Music Master》 on the winter solstice prescribes the Circular Mound above ground and says 'honor the spirit of Heaven'; on the summer solstice prescribes the Square Mound in the marsh and says 'honor the spirit of Earth.'

sentences.zh: 天地分祀，從來久矣。

translations.literal: Separate sacrifice to Heaven and Earth has been the case from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth have been worshipped separately from of old.

sentences.zh: 故宋儒葉時之言曰：「郊丘分合之說，當以《周禮》為定。

translations.literal: Therefore the Song Confucian Ye Shi said: "On the question of separate or joint suburban and mound sacrifice, the 《Rites of Zhou》 should be taken as definitive.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Song scholar Ye Shi said: "On whether suburban and mound sacrifices should be separate or joint, the 《Rites of Zhou》 should be definitive.

sentences.zh: 」今議者既以大社為祭地，則南郊自不當祭皇地祇，何又以分祭為不可也？

translations.literal: Now those who debate already take the great god of soil as sacrifice to Earth—then the southern suburb naturally ought not sacrifice to the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth; why then do they say separate sacrifice is impossible?
translations.idiomatic: If debaters already take the great god of soil as sacrifice to Earth, then the southern suburb naturally ought not worship the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth—why then do they say separate sacrifice is impossible?

sentences.zh: 合祭之說，實自莽始，漢之前皆主分祭，而漢之後亦間有之。

translations.literal: The doctrine of joint sacrifice in fact began with Mang; before Han all upheld separate sacrifice, and after Han there were also occasional cases.
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine of joint sacrifice in fact began with Wang Mang; before Han all upheld separate sacrifice, and after Han there were occasional cases as well.

sentences.zh: 宋元豐一議，元祐再議，紹聖三議，皆主合祭，而卒不可移者，以郊賚之費，每傾府藏，故省約安簡便耳，亦未嘗以分祭為禮也。

translations.literal: The first debate in Yuanfeng of Song, the second in Yuanyou, the third in Shaosheng—all upheld joint sacrifice, yet in the end it could not be moved because the gifts at suburban sacrifice depleted the treasury each time; it was merely economy and convenience, and they never took separate sacrifice as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The first debate in Yuanfeng, the second in Yuanyou, the third in Shaosheng—all upheld joint sacrifice, yet in the end it could not be changed because the gifts at suburban sacrifice depleted the treasury each time; it was merely economy and convenience, and they never took separate sacrifice as the proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 今之議者，往往以太祖之制為嫌為懼。

translations.literal: Those who debate now often take the Founding Emperor's institution as grounds for objection and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debate now often shrink from challenging the Founding Emperor's institution.

sentences.zh: 然知合祭乃太祖之定制，為不可改，而不知分祭固太祖之初制，為可復。

translations.literal: Yet they know that joint sacrifice was the Founding Emperor's settled custom and cannot be changed, but do not know that separate sacrifice was the Founding Emperor's original institution and can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: They know that joint sacrifice was the Founding Emperor's settled custom and cannot be changed, but do not know that separate sacrifice was his original institution and can be restored.

sentences.zh: 知《大祀文》乃太祖之明訓，為不可背，而不知《存心錄》固太祖之著典，為可遵。

translations.literal: They know the 《Grand Sacrifice Text》 was the Founding Emperor's clear instruction and cannot be violated, but do not know that the 《Record of Preserving the Heart》 is the Founding Emperor's authored code and can be followed.
translations.idiomatic: They know the 《Grand Sacrifice Text》 was the Founding Emperor's clear instruction and cannot be violated, but do not know that the 《Record of Preserving the Heart》 is his authored code and can be followed.

sentences.zh: 且皆太祖之制也，從其禮之是者而已。

translations.literal: Both are the Founding Emperor's institutions—one need only follow whichever ritual is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Both are the Founding Emperor's institutions—one need only follow whichever ritual is correct.

sentences.zh: 敬天法祖，無二道也。

translations.literal: Revering Heaven and respecting ancestors are not two ways.
translations.idiomatic: Revering Heaven and honoring ancestors are not two paths.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》一書，硃子以為周公輔導成王，垂法後世，用意最深切，何可誣以莽之偽為耶？

translations.literal: The book 《Rites of Zhou》—Zhu Xi held that the Duke of Zhou in assisting and guiding King Cheng left laws for later generations with the deepest intent—how can it be slandered as Mang's forgery?
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou》—Zhu Xi held that the Duke of Zhou in guiding King Cheng left laws for later generations with the deepest intent—how can it be slandered as Wang Mang's forgery?

sentences.zh: 且合祭以後配地，實自莽始。

translations.literal: Moreover joint sacrifice with Queen Earth as accompaniment in fact began with Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover joint sacrifice with Queen Earth as accompaniment in fact began with Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 莽既偽為是書，何不削去圜丘、方丘之制，天神地祇之祭，而自為一說耶？

translations.literal: If Mang forged this book, why did he not excise the regulations for Circular Mound and Square Mound and sacrifice to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, and compose a doctrine of his own?
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Mang forged this book, why did he not excise the regulations for the Circular Mound and Square Mound and sacrifice to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, and compose a doctrine of his own?

sentences.zh: 於是禮部集上羣臣所議郊禮，奏曰：「主分祭者，都御史汪鋐等八十二人，主分祭而以慎重成憲及時未可為言者，大學士張璁等八十四人，主分祭而以山川壇為方丘者，尚書李瓚等二十六人，主合祭而不以分祭為非者，尚書方獻夫等二百六人，無可否者，英國公張侖等一百九十八人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites collected and submitted officials' views on suburban ritual, memorializing: "Those who uphold separate sacrifice: Censor-in-Chief Wang Wo and eighty-two others; those who uphold separate sacrifice but say that the completed statutes should be respected and the time is not yet ripe: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong and eighty-four others; those who uphold separate sacrifice but take the Mountains-and-Rivers Altar as the Square Mound: Minister Li Zan and twenty-six others; those who uphold joint sacrifice without deeming separate sacrifice wrong: Minister Fang Xianfu and two hundred six others; those who expressed no opinion: Duke of Ying Zhang Lun and one hundred ninety-eight others.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites collected officials' views on suburban ritual and memorialized: "Those who uphold separate sacrifice: Censor-in-Chief Wang Wo and eighty-two others; those who uphold separate sacrifice but say the completed statutes should be respected and the time is not yet ripe: Grand Secretary Zhang Cong and eighty-four others; those who uphold separate sacrifice but take the Mountains-and-Rivers Altar as the Square Mound: Minister Li Zan and twenty-six others; those who uphold joint sacrifice without deeming separate sacrifice wrong: Minister Fang Xianfu and two hundred six others; those who expressed no opinion: Duke of Ying Zhang Lun and one hundred ninety-eight others.

sentences.zh: 臣等祗奉敕諭，折衷眾論。

translations.literal: We, your ministers, reverently received Your Majesty's command and weighed the multitude of opinions.
translations.idiomatic: We, your ministers, reverently received Your Majesty's command and weighed the multitude of opinions.

sentences.zh: 分祀之義，合於古禮，但壇壝一建，工役浩繁。

translations.literal: The principle of separate sacrifice conforms to ancient ritual, but once the altars are built, the labor is immense.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of separate sacrifice conforms to ancient ritual, but once the altars are built the labor is immense.

sentences.zh: 《禮》，屋祭曰帝，夫既稱昊天上帝，則當屋祭。

translations.literal: The 《Rites》: sacrifice under a roof is called the Emperor—since [Heaven] is called August Heaven, Sovereign on High, it ought to be sacrificed to under a roof.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites》 says sacrifice under a roof is called the Emperor—since Heaven is called August Heaven, Sovereign on High, it ought to be worshipped under a roof.

sentences.zh: 宜仍於大祀殿專祀上帝，改山川壇為地壇，以專祀皇地祇。

translations.literal: It is fitting to continue exclusive sacrifice to the Sovereign on High in the Grand Sacrifice Hall, and to convert the Mountains-and-Rivers Altar into an Earth Altar for exclusive sacrifice to the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to continue exclusive worship of the Sovereign on High in the Grand Sacrifice Hall and to convert the Mountains-and-Rivers Altar into an Earth Altar for exclusive worship of the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth.

sentences.zh: 既無創建之勞，行禮亦便。

translations.literal: There would be no labor of new construction, and performing the ritual would also be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: This would avoid new construction and make the rites easier to perform.

sentences.zh: 」帝復諭當遵皇祖舊制，露祭於壇，分南北郊，以二至日行事。

translations.literal: The Emperor again instructed that the imperial ancestor's old system should be followed: open-air sacrifice on the altar, separate southern and northern suburbs, and performance on the two solstice days.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again instructed that the imperial ancestor's old system should be followed: open-air sacrifice on the altar, separate southern and northern suburbs, and performance on the two solstice days.

sentences.zh: 言乃奏曰：「南郊合祀，循襲已久，硃子所謂千五六百年無人整理。

translations.literal: Yan then memorialized: "Joint sacrifice at the southern suburb has been followed for so long that, as Zhu Xi said, for fifteen or sixteen hundred years no one has put it in order.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then memorialized: "Joint sacrifice at the southern suburb has been followed so long that, as Zhu Xi said, for fifteen or sixteen hundred years no one has set it right.

sentences.zh: 而陛下獨破千古之謬，一理舉行，誠可謂建諸天地而不悖者也。」

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty alone has broken the error of a thousand ages and carried out the single correct principle—truly this may be called establishing [rites] between Heaven and Earth without contradiction."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty alone has broken the error of a thousand ages and carried out the single correct principle—truly this may be called establishing rites between Heaven and Earth without contradiction."

sentences.zh: 已而命戶、禮、工三部偕言等詣南郊相擇。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he ordered the Ministries of Revenue, Rites, and Works, together with Yan and others, to go to the southern suburb to select a site.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he ordered the Ministries of Revenue, Rites, and Works, together with Yan and others, to go to the southern suburb to select a site.

sentences.zh: 南天門外有自然之丘，咸謂舊丘地位偏東，不宜襲用。

translations.literal: Outside the Southern Heavenly Gate there was a natural mound; all said the old mound's position was too far east and should not be reused.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Southern Heavenly Gate there was a natural mound; all agreed the old mound lay too far east and should not be reused.

sentences.zh: 禮臣欲於具服殿少南為圜丘。

translations.literal: The ritual officials wished to place the Circular Mound slightly south of the Robing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials wished to place the Circular Mound slightly south of the Robing Hall.

sentences.zh: 言復奏曰：「圜丘祀天，宜即高敞，以展對越之敬。

translations.literal: Yan again memorialized: "The Circular Mound sacrifices to Heaven and ought to be lofty and open, to display the reverence of facing and responding.
translations.idiomatic: Yan again memorialized: "The Circular Mound worships Heaven and ought to stand lofty and open, to display the reverence of facing and responding.

sentences.zh: 大祀殿享帝，宜即清閟，以盡昭事之誠。

translations.literal: The Grand Sacrifice Hall honors the Emperor and ought to be secluded and quiet, to fulfill fully the sincerity of bright service.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Sacrifice Hall honors the Emperor and ought to be secluded and quiet, to fulfill fully the sincerity of bright service.

sentences.zh: 二祭時義不同，則壇殿相去，亦宜有所區別。

translations.literal: The two sacrifices differ in seasonal meaning; then the distance between altar and hall ought also to be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The two sacrifices differ in seasonal meaning; the distance between altar and hall ought therefore to be distinguished as well.

sentences.zh: 乞於具服殿稍南為大祀殿，而圜丘更移於前，體勢峻極，可與大祀殿等。

translations.literal: I beg that the Grand Sacrifice Hall be placed slightly south of the Robing Hall, and the Circular Mound moved further forward, its form towering and lofty, equal to the Grand Sacrifice Hall.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Grand Sacrifice Hall be placed slightly south of the Robing Hall and the Circular Mound moved further forward, its form towering and lofty, equal to the Grand Sacrifice Hall.

translations.literal: An edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 於是作圜丘，是年十月工成。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Circular Mound was built; in the tenth month of that year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Circular Mound was built; in the tenth month of that year the work was completed.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，北郊及東、西郊，亦以次告成，而分祀之制遂定。

translations.literal: The next summer the northern suburb and the eastern and western suburbs were also completed in turn, and the system of separate sacrifice was thus fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer the northern suburb and the eastern and western suburbs were also completed in turn, and the system of separate sacrifice was thus fixed.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，大學士張居正等輯《郊祀新舊圖考》進呈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli, Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and others compiled the 《Illustrated Study of Old and New Suburban Sacrifices》 and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 3 Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and others compiled the 《Illustrated Study of Old and New Suburban Sacrifices》 and presented it.

sentences.zh: 舊禮者，太祖所定。

translations.literal: The old ritual was that fixed by the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The old ritual was that fixed by the Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 新禮者，世宗所定也。

translations.literal: The new ritual was that fixed by the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The new ritual was that fixed by the Jiajing Emperor.

sentences.zh: ○郊祀配位

translations.literal: ○ Matched seats at suburban sacrifices
translations.idiomatic: Matched Seats at Suburban Sacrifices

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，始有事於南郊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, sacrifice at the southern suburb was first performed.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 sacrifice at the southern suburb was first performed.

sentences.zh: 有司議配祀。

translations.literal: The responsible officials discussed matched sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials discussed matched sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太祖謙讓不許，親為文告太廟曰：「歷代有天下者，皆以祖配天。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor declined in humility and would not permit it; he personally composed a text announcing to the Grand Temple: "Throughout the ages those who possessed the realm have all matched an ancestor with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor declined in humility and would not permit it; he personally composed a text announcing to the Grand Temple: "Throughout the ages those who possessed the realm have all matched an ancestor with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣獨不敢者，以臣功業有未就，政治有闕失。

translations.literal: Your servant alone dares not, because your servant's achievements are not yet complete and governance has shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant alone dares not, because your servant's achievements are not yet complete and governance has shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 去年上天垂戒，有聲東南，雷火焚舟擊殿吻，早暮兢惕，恐無以承上帝好生之德，故不敢輒奉以配。

translations.literal: Last year Heaven sent down a warning: a sound in the southeast, thunder and fire burning boats and striking the hall's ridge ornaments; morning and evening I was vigilant in fear, lest I be unable to receive August Heaven's virtue of cherishing life—therefore I dare not rashly offer [myself] as match.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Heaven sent down a warning: a sound in the southeast, thunder and fire burning boats and striking the hall's ridge ornaments; morning and evening I was vigilant in fear, lest I be unable to receive August Heaven's virtue of cherishing life—therefore I dare not rashly offer myself as match.

sentences.zh: 惟祖神與天通，上帝有問，願以臣所行奏帝前，善惡無隱。

translations.literal: Only the ancestral spirit communicates with Heaven; if August Heaven has questions, I wish that what your servant has done be reported before the Emperor, good and evil without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ancestral spirit communicates with Heaven; if August Heaven has questions, I wish that what your servant has done be reported before the Emperor, good and evil without concealment.

sentences.zh: 候南郊竣事，臣率百司恭詣廟廷，告成大禮，以共用上帝之錫福。

translations.literal: When the southern suburban rites are concluded, your servant will lead the hundred offices in reverent attendance at the temple court to announce the completion of the great ritual, that together we may share August Heaven's bestowed blessings.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern suburban rites are concluded, your servant will lead the hundred offices in reverent attendance at the temple court to announce the completion of the great ritual, that together we may share August Heaven's bestowed blessings.

sentences.zh: 」明年夏至，將祀方丘，羣臣復請。

translations.literal: The next year at the summer solstice, when the Square Mound was to be sacrificed to, the officials again requested.
translations.idiomatic: The next year at the summer solstice, when the Square Mound was to be worshipped, the officials again requested.

sentences.zh: 乃奉皇考仁祖淳皇帝配天於圜丘。

translations.literal: Thereupon the deceased father, the Pure Emperor Renzu, was offered as match with Heaven at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the deceased father, the Pure Emperor Renzu, was offered as match with Heaven at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 明年祀方丘，亦如之。

translations.literal: The next year at sacrifice to the Square Mound, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The next year at worship at the Square Mound, it was likewise.

sentences.zh: 建文元年，改奉太祖配。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen, sacrifice was changed to match the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen 1 sacrifice was changed to match the Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 洪熙改元，敕曰：「太祖受命上天，肇興皇業。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Hongxi, an edict said: "The Founding Emperor received mandate from Heaven and inaugurated the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: At the change of reign to Hongxi, an edict said: "The Founding Emperor received mandate from Heaven and inaugurated the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 太宗中興宗社，再奠寰區。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor revived the altars of state and again settled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong Emperor revived the altars of state and again settled the realm.

sentences.zh: 聖德神功，咸配天地。

translations.literal: Their sagely virtue and divine achievement both match Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Their sagely virtue and divine achievement both match Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰，『殷薦上帝，以配祖考』。

translations.literal: The 《Changes》 says: 'The Yin offer sacrifice to August Heaven, matching the ancestral fathers.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Changes》 says: 'The Yin offer sacrifice to August Heaven, matching the ancestral fathers.'

sentences.zh: 朕崇敬祖考，永惟一心。

translations.literal: We revere and honor our ancestral fathers with undivided heart forever.
translations.idiomatic: We revere and honor our ancestral fathers with undivided heart forever.

sentences.zh: 正月十五日，大祀天地神祇，奉皇祖、皇考以配。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the first month, at the Grand Sacrifice to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, we offer the imperial grandfather and imperial father as match.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the first month, at the Grand Sacrifice to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, we offer the imperial grandfather and imperial father as match.

sentences.zh: 」遂於郊祀前告太廟及几筵，請太祖、太宗並配。

translations.literal: Thereupon before the suburban sacrifice he announced to the Grand Temple and spirit tablets, requesting that the Founding and Taizong Emperors be jointly matched.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon before the suburban sacrifice he announced to the Grand Temple and spirit tablets, requesting that the Founding and Taizong Emperors be jointly matched.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，給事中夏言上疏言：「太祖、太宗並配，父子同列，稽之經旨，未能無疑。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, Supervising Secretary Xia Yan submitted a memorial stating: "The Founding and Taizong Emperors jointly matched, father and son in the same row—examined against the classics' intent, doubt cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 Supervising Secretary Xia Yan submitted a memorial stating: "The Founding and Taizong Emperors jointly matched, father and son in the same row—examined against the classics' intent, doubt cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 臣謂周人郊祀后稷以配天，太祖足當之。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the Zhou people sacrificed to Hou Ji in the suburbs to match Heaven—the Founding Emperor fully suffices for this.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the Zhou people sacrificed to Hou Ji in the suburbs to match Heaven—the Founding Emperor fully suffices for this.

sentences.zh: 宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝，太宗足當之。

translations.literal: In the ancestral temple they honored King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign on High—the Taizong Emperor fully suffices for this.
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple they honored King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Sovereign on High—the Taizong Emperor fully suffices for this.

sentences.zh: 」禮臣集議，以為二祖配享，百有餘年，不宜一旦輕改。

translations.literal: The ritual officials assembled in discussion and held that the two ancestors had been matched in enjoyment for more than a hundred years and ought not be lightly changed at once.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials assembled in discussion and held that the two ancestors had been matched in enjoyment for more than a hundred years and ought not be lightly changed at once.

sentences.zh: 帝降敕諭，欲於二至日奉太祖配南、北郊，歲首奉太宗配上帝於大祀殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict of instruction, wishing on the two solstice days to offer the Founding Emperor as match at the southern and northern suburbs, and at the year's beginning to offer the Taizong Emperor as match with the Sovereign on High in the Grand Sacrifice Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an edict of instruction, wishing on the two solstice days to offer the Founding Emperor as match at the southern and northern suburbs, and at the year's beginning to offer the Taizong Emperor as match with the Sovereign on High in the Grand Sacrifice Hall.

sentences.zh: 於是大學士張璁、翟鑾等言，二祖分配，於義未協，且錄仁宗年撰敕諭並告廟文以進。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Secretaries Zhang Cong and Zhai Luan and others said that allocating the two ancestors was not in accord with principle, and they recorded and submitted the edict of instruction and temple announcement composed in the Renzong era.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Grand Secretaries Zhang Cong and Zhai Luan and others said that allocating the two ancestors was not in accord with principle, and they recorded and submitted the edict of instruction and temple announcement composed in the Renzong era.

sentences.zh: 帝復命集議於東閣，皆以為：「太廟之祀，列聖昭穆相向，無嫌並列。

translations.literal: The Emperor again ordered discussion assembled in the Eastern Pavilion; all held: "In sacrifice at the Grand Temple the sage emperors face one another in zhao and mu order—there is no objection to placing them side by side.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again ordered discussion assembled in the Eastern Pavilion; all held: "In sacrifice at the Grand Temple the sage emperors face one another in zhao and mu order—there is no objection to placing them side by side.

sentences.zh: 況太祖、太宗，功德並隆，圜丘、大祀殿所祀，均之為天，則配天之祖，不宜闕一。

translations.literal: Moreover the Founding and Taizong Emperors' merit and virtue are equally lofty; what the Circular Mound and Grand Sacrifice Hall sacrifice to are equally Heaven—then the ancestors who match Heaven ought not lack one.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Founding and Taizong Emperors' merit and virtue are equally lofty; what the Circular Mound and Grand Sacrifice Hall worship are equally Heaven—then the ancestors who match Heaven ought not lack one.

sentences.zh: 臣等竊議南、北郊及大祀殿，每祭皆宜二祖並配。

translations.literal: We your ministers venture to discuss that at the southern and northern suburbs and the Grand Sacrifice Hall, at each sacrifice both ancestors ought to be jointly matched.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers venture to discuss that at the southern and northern suburbs and the Grand Sacrifice Hall, at each sacrifice both ancestors ought to be jointly matched.

sentences.zh: 」帝終以並配非禮，諭閣臣講求。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately held that joint matching was not ritual and instructed the Grand Secretariat members to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ultimately held that joint matching was not ritual and instructed the Grand Secretariat members to investigate.

sentences.zh: 璁等言：「《禮》曰：『有其舉之，莫敢廢也。

translations.literal: Cong and others said: "The 《Rites》 says: 'Where there is an established practice, none dares abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and others said: "The 《Rites》 says: 'Where there is an established practice, none dares abolish it.

sentences.zh: 』凡祭盡然，況祖宗配享大典？

translations.literal: ' This applies to all sacrifices—how much more to the great ceremony of matching ancestors in enjoyment?
translations.idiomatic: ' This applies to all sacrifices—how much more to the great ceremony of matching ancestors in enjoyment?

sentences.zh: 且古者郊與明堂異地，故可分配。

translations.literal: Moreover in antiquity the suburb and Bright Hall were in different places, therefore allocation was possible.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in antiquity the suburb and Bright Hall were in different places, therefore allocation was possible.

sentences.zh: 今圜丘、大祀殿同兆南郊，冬至禮行於報而太宗不與，孟春禮行於祈而太祖不與，心實有所不安。

translations.literal: Now the Circular Mound and Grand Sacrifice Hall share the southern suburban site; at the winter solstice the ritual of reporting is performed yet the Taizong Emperor is not included, and in the first month of spring the ritual of prayer is performed yet the Founding Emperor is not included—the heart truly feels uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Circular Mound and Grand Sacrifice Hall share the southern suburban site; at the winter solstice the ritual of reporting is performed yet the Taizong Emperor is not included, and in the first month of spring the ritual of prayer is performed yet the Founding Emperor is not included—the heart truly feels uneasy.

sentences.zh: 」帝復報曰：「萬物本乎天，人本乎祖。

translations.literal: The Emperor again replied: "The ten thousand things root in Heaven; humanity roots in ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again replied: "The ten thousand things root in Heaven; humanity roots in ancestors.

sentences.zh: 天惟一天，祖亦惟一祖。

translations.literal: Heaven is only one Heaven; ancestors are also only one ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is only one Heaven; ancestors are also only one ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故大報天之祀，止當以高皇帝配。

translations.literal: Therefore at the great sacrifice reporting to Heaven, only the High Emperor ought to be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at the great sacrifice reporting to Heaven, only the High Emperor ought to be matched.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝功德，豈不可配天？

translations.literal: The Wén Emperor's merit and virtue—how could he not match Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: The Wén Emperor's merit and virtue—how could he not match Heaven?

sentences.zh: 但開天立極，本高皇帝肇之耳。

translations.literal: But opening Heaven and establishing the pole fundamentally was begun by the High Emperor alone.
translations.idiomatic: But opening Heaven and establishing the pole was fundamentally begun by the High Emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 如周之王業，武王實成之，而配天止以后稷，配上帝止以文王，當時未聞爭辨功德也。

translations.literal: As with the Zhou royal enterprise, King Wu truly completed it, yet matching Heaven was only with Hou Ji and matching the Sovereign on High only with King Wen—at the time no dispute over merit was heard.
translations.idiomatic: As with the Zhou royal enterprise, King Wu truly completed it, yet matching Heaven was only with Hou Ji and matching the Sovereign on High only with King Wen—at the time no dispute over merit was heard.

sentences.zh: 」因命寢其議。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the discussion suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered the discussion suspended.

sentences.zh: 已而夏言復疏言：「虞、夏、殷、周之郊，惟配一祖。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xia Yan again submitted a memorial stating: "In the suburban sacrifices of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, only one ancestor was matched.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Xia Yan again submitted a memorial stating: "In the suburban sacrifices of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, only one ancestor was matched.

sentences.zh: 後儒穿鑿，分郊丘為二，及誤解《大易》配考、《孝經》嚴父之義。

translations.literal: Later Confucians forced interpretations, splitting suburban and mound sacrifice into two, and misreading the meaning of matching the father in the 《Great Changes》 and honoring the father in the 《Classic of Filial Piety》.
translations.idiomatic: Later Confucians forced interpretations, splitting suburban and mound sacrifice into two, and misreading the meaning of matching the father in the 《Great Changes》 and honoring the father in the 《Classic of Filial Piety》.

sentences.zh: 以致唐、宋變古，乃有二祖並侑，三帝並配之事。

translations.literal: This led Tang and Song to alter antiquity, producing the affairs of two ancestors jointly accompanied and three emperors jointly matched.
translations.idiomatic: This led Tang and Song to alter antiquity, producing the affairs of two ancestors jointly accompanied and three emperors jointly matched.

sentences.zh: 望斷自宸衷，依前敕旨。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will decide from the imperial heart and follow the previous edict of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will decide from the imperial heart and follow the previous edict of instruction.

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「禮臣前引太廟不嫌一堂。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied: "The ritual officials previously cited that the Grand Temple does not object to one hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "The ritual officials previously cited that the Grand Temple does not object to one hall.

sentences.zh: 夫祀帝與享先不同，此說無當。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Emperor and enjoyment of ancestors differ—this argument is inapplicable.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Emperor and enjoyment of ancestors differ—this argument is inapplicable.

sentences.zh: 」仍命申議。

translations.literal: He still ordered further discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered further discussion.

sentences.zh: 於是禮臣復上議：「南北郊雖曰祖制，實今日新創。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ritual officials again submitted discussion: "Although the southern and northern suburbs are called the ancestral institution, they are in fact newly created today.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ritual officials again submitted discussion: "Although the southern and northern suburbs are called the ancestral institution, they are in fact newly created today.

sentences.zh: 請如聖諭，俱奉太祖獨配。

translations.literal: We request that as in the sage instruction, the Founding Emperor alone be offered as match at both.
translations.idiomatic: We request that as in the sage instruction, the Founding Emperor alone be offered as match at both.

sentences.zh: 至大祀殿則太祖所創，今乃不得侑享於中，恐太宗未安，宜仍奉二祖並配。

translations.literal: As for the Grand Sacrifice Hall, it was created by the Founding Emperor; now he cannot be accompanied in enjoyment within it—we fear the Taizong Emperor would be unsettled; it is fitting still to offer both ancestors jointly matched.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Grand Sacrifice Hall, it was created by the Founding Emperor; now he cannot be accompanied in enjoyment within it—we fear the Taizong Emperor would be unsettled; it is fitting still to offer both ancestors jointly matched.

sentences.zh: 」遂依擬行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: ○郊祀儀注

translations.literal: ○ Regulations for suburban sacrifices
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for Suburban Sacrifices

sentences.zh: 洪武元年冬至，祀昊天上帝於圜丘。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of the first year of Hongwu, August Heaven, Sovereign on High was sacrificed to at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of Hongwu 1, August Heaven, Sovereign on High was worshipped at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 先期，皇帝散齋四日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the Emperor observed dispersed fasting for four days and concentrated fasting for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand, the Emperor observed dispersed fasting for four days and concentrated fasting for three days.

sentences.zh: 前祀二日，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍省牲器。

translations.literal: Two days before the sacrifice, the Emperor wore the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe to inspect the victims and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before the sacrifice, the Emperor wore the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe to inspect the victims and vessels.

sentences.zh: 次日，有司陳設。

translations.literal: The next day, the responsible officials arranged the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the responsible officials arranged the offerings.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，清晨車駕至大次，太常卿奏中嚴，皇帝服袞冕。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, at dawn the imperial carriage arrived at the great tent; the Minister of Ceremonies reported mid-strictness, and the Emperor donned the dragon robe and cap.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice, at dawn the imperial carriage arrived at the great tent; the Minister of Ceremonies reported mid-strictness, and the Emperor donned the dragon robe and cap.

sentences.zh: 奏外辦，皇帝入就位，贊禮唱迎神。

translations.literal: He reported outer readiness; the Emperor entered and took his place; the ritual intoner chanted welcoming the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He reported outer readiness; the Emperor entered and took his place; the ritual intoner chanted welcoming the spirits.

sentences.zh: 協律郎舉麾奏《中和之曲》。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Harmonious Equilibrium》 suite.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Harmonious Equilibrium》 suite.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱燔柴，郊社令升煙，燔全犢於燎壇。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted burning firewood; the suburban and soil-altar commissioner raised smoke and burned a whole calf on the blaze altar.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted burning firewood; the suburban and soil-altar commissioner raised smoke and burned a whole calf on the blaze altar.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱請行禮，太常卿奏有司謹具，請行事。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted requesting performance of the ritual; the Minister of Ceremonies reported that the officials had reverently prepared everything and requested commencement.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted requesting performance of the ritual; the Minister of Ceremonies reported that the officials had reverently prepared everything and requested commencement.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再拜，皇太子及在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Emperor bowed twice; the Crown Prince and all officials in attendance likewise bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bowed twice; the Crown Prince and all officials in attendance likewise bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱奠玉帛，皇帝詣盥洗位。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted presenting jade and silks; the Emperor proceeded to the hand-washing place.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted presenting jade and silks; the Emperor proceeded to the hand-washing place.

sentences.zh: 太常卿贊曰：「前期齋戒，今辰奉祭，加其清潔，以對神明。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies intoned: "Having fasted beforehand, at this hour we perform sacrifice—increase your purity to face the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies intoned: "Having fasted beforehand, at this hour we perform sacrifice—increase your purity to face the spirits.

sentences.zh: 」皇帝搢圭，盥手，帨手。

translations.literal: The Emperor inserted the scepter, washed his hands, and dried his hands.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor inserted the scepter, washed his hands, and dried his hands.

sentences.zh: 出圭，升壇。

translations.literal: He withdrew the scepter and ascended the altar.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew the scepter and ascended the altar.

sentences.zh: 太常卿贊曰：「神明在上，整肅威儀。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies intoned: "The spirits are above—compose your dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies intoned: "The spirits are above—compose your dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 」升自午陛。

translations.literal: He ascended by the noon stair.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended by the noon stair.

sentences.zh: 協律郎舉麾奏《凝和之曲》。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Concentrated Harmony》 suite.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Concentrated Harmony》 suite.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣昊天上帝神位前跪，搢圭，三上香，奠玉帛，出圭，再拜復位。

translations.literal: The Emperor proceeded before the spirit seat of August Heaven, Sovereign on High, knelt, inserted the scepter, offered incense three times, presented jade and silks, withdrew the scepter, bowed twice, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor proceeded before the spirit seat of August Heaven, Sovereign on High, knelt, inserted the scepter, offered incense three times, presented jade and silks, withdrew the scepter, bowed twice, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱進俎，協律郎舉麾奏《凝和之曲》。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted presenting the meat trays; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Concentrated Harmony》 suite.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted presenting the meat trays; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Concentrated Harmony》 suite.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣神位前，搢圭奠俎，出圭，復位。

translations.literal: The Emperor proceeded before the spirit seat, inserted the scepter and presented the meat tray, withdrew the scepter, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor proceeded before the spirit seat, inserted the scepter and presented the meat tray, withdrew the scepter, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱行初獻禮。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted performing the first offering ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted performing the first offering ritual.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣爵洗位，搢圭，滌爵，拭爵，以爵授執事者，出圭。

translations.literal: The Emperor proceeded to the cup-washing place, inserted the scepter, rinsed the cup, wiped the cup, handed the cup to the attendant, and withdrew the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor proceeded to the cup-washing place, inserted the scepter, rinsed the cup, wiped the cup, handed the cup to the attendant, and withdrew the scepter.

sentences.zh: 詣酒尊年，搢圭，執爵，受泛齊，以爵授執事者，出圭。

translations.literal: He proceeded to the wine vessel, inserted the scepter, took the cup, received the first-fermented wine, handed the cup to the attendant, and withdrew the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded to the wine vessel, inserted the scepter, took the cup, received the first-fermented wine, handed the cup to the attendant, and withdrew the scepter.

sentences.zh: 協律郎舉麾奏《壽和之曲》、《武功之舞》。

translations.literal: The pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Longevity and Harmony》 suite and the 《Martial Merit》 dance.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Longevity and Harmony》 suite and the 《Martial Merit》 dance.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣神位前跪，搢圭，上香，祭酒，奠爵，出圭。

translations.literal: The Emperor proceeded before the spirit seat, knelt, inserted the scepter, offered incense, poured the libation, presented the cup, and withdrew the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor proceeded before the spirit seat, knelt, inserted the scepter, offered incense, poured the libation, presented the cup, and withdrew the scepter.

sentences.zh: 讀祝官捧祝跪讀訖，皇帝俯伏，興，再拜，復位。

translations.literal: The prayer-reading officer held the prayer, knelt, and finished reading; the Emperor prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer-reading officer held the prayer, knelt, and finished reading; the Emperor prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，酌醴齊，樂奏《豫和之曲》、《文德之舞》。

translations.literal: At the second offering, the second-fermented wine was poured; music performed the 《Abundant Harmony》 suite and the 《Civil Virtue》 dance.
translations.idiomatic: At the second offering, the second-fermented wine was poured; music performed the 《Abundant Harmony》 suite and the 《Civil Virtue》 dance.

sentences.zh: 終獻，酌盎齊，樂奏《熙和之曲》、《文德之舞》。

translations.literal: At the final offering, the clear-fermented wine was poured; music performed the 《Radiant Harmony》 suite and the 《Civil Virtue》 dance.
translations.idiomatic: At the final offering, the clear-fermented wine was poured; music performed the 《Radiant Harmony》 suite and the 《Civil Virtue》 dance.

sentences.zh: 儀並同初獻，但不用祝。

translations.literal: The ritual was the same as the first offering, but without the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual was the same as the first offering, but without the prayer.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱飲福受胙，皇帝升壇，至飲福位，再拜，跪，搢圭。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted drinking the blessing and receiving the sacrificial meat; the Emperor ascended the altar, reached the blessing-drinking place, bowed twice, knelt, and inserted the scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted drinking the blessing and receiving the sacrificial meat; the Emperor ascended the altar, reached the blessing-drinking place, bowed twice, knelt, and inserted the scepter.

sentences.zh: 奉爵官酌福酒跪進，太常卿贊曰：「惟此酒餚，神之所與，賜以福慶，億兆同沾。

translations.literal: The cup-bearing officer poured the blessing wine, knelt, and presented it; the Minister of Ceremonies intoned: "Only this wine and viands are what the spirits bestow, granting blessing and felicity that the hundred millions may all share."
translations.idiomatic: The cup-bearing officer poured the blessing wine, knelt, and presented it; the Minister of Ceremonies intoned: "Only this wine and viands are what the spirits bestow, granting blessing and felicity that the hundred millions may all share."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝受爵，祭酒，飲福酒，以爵置於坫。

translations.literal: " The Emperor received the cup, poured the libation, drank the blessing wine, and placed the cup on the offering stand.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor received the cup, poured the libation, drank the blessing wine, and placed the cup on the offering stand.

sentences.zh: 奉胙官奉胙跪進，皇帝受胙，以授執事者，出圭，俯伏，興，再拜，復位。

translations.literal: The sacrificial-meat officer presented the sacrificial meat, knelt, and advanced it; the Emperor received the meat, handed it to the attendant, withdrew the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial-meat officer presented the sacrificial meat, knelt, and advanced it; the Emperor received the meat, handed it to the attendant, withdrew the scepter, prostrated himself, rose, bowed twice, and returned to his place.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以下在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: From the Crown Prince down, all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: From the Crown Prince down, all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱徹豆，協律郎舉麾奏《雍和之曲》，掌祭官徹豆。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted withdrawing the beans; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Harmonious Tranquility》 suite; the sacrifice officers withdrew the beans.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted withdrawing the beans; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Harmonious Tranquility》 suite; the sacrifice officers withdrew the beans.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱送神，協律郎舉麾奏《安和之曲》。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted escorting the spirits; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Peaceful Harmony》 suite.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted escorting the spirits; the pitch-regulating officer raised the baton and performed the 《Peaceful Harmony》 suite.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再拜，皇太子以下在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Emperor bowed twice; from the Crown Prince down, all officials in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bowed twice; from the Crown Prince down, all officials in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊禮唱讀祝官奉祝，奉幣官奉幣，掌祭官取饌及爵酒，各詣燎所。

translations.literal: The ritual intoner chanted; the prayer-reading officer bore the prayer, the silk-offering officer bore the silks, and the sacrifice officers took the viands and cup-wine, each proceeding to the blaze site.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual intoner chanted; the prayer-reading officer bore the prayer, the silk-offering officer bore the silks, and the sacrifice officers took the viands and cup-wine, each proceeding to the blaze site.

sentences.zh: 唱望燎，皇帝至望燎位。

translations.literal: They chanted gazing at the blaze; the Emperor reached the blaze-gazing place.
translations.idiomatic: They chanted gazing at the blaze; the Emperor reached the blaze-gazing place.

sentences.zh: 半燎，太常卿奏禮畢，皇帝還大次，解嚴。

translations.literal: When the blaze was half consumed, the Minister of Ceremonies reported the rite complete; the Emperor returned to the great tent and the strict guard was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the blaze was half consumed, the Minister of Ceremonies reported the rite complete; the Emperor returned to the great tent and the strict guard was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二年夏至，祀皇地祇於方丘，其儀並同。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice of the second year, the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth was sacrificed to at the Square Mound; the ritual was entirely the same.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice of the second year, the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth was worshipped at the Square Mound; the ritual was otherwise the same.

sentences.zh: 惟迎神後瘞毛血，祭畢，奉牲帛祝饌而埋之，與郊天異。

translations.literal: Only after welcoming the spirits were the hair and blood buried; when the sacrifice was complete, the victims, silks, prayer, and viands were taken and buried—this differed from suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only after welcoming the spirits were the hair and blood buried; when the sacrifice was complete, the victims, silks, prayer, and viands were taken and buried—this differed from suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其冬，奉仁祖配天於南郊，儀同元年。

translations.literal: That winter, Founder Renzu was offered as match with Heaven at the southern suburb; the ritual was the same as the first year.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Founder Renzu was offered as match with Heaven at the southern suburb; the ritual was the same as the first year.

sentences.zh: 其奠玉帛、進俎、三獻，皆先詣上帝前，次詣仁祖神位前，行禮亦如之，惟不用玉。

translations.literal: For presenting jade and silks, advancing the trays, and the three offerings, all first proceeded before the Sovereign on High, then before Founder Renzu's spirit seat, performing the rites likewise—only jade was not used.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting jade and silks, advancing the trays, and the three offerings, all first proceeded before the Sovereign on High, then before Founder Renzu's spirit seat, performing the rites likewise—only jade was not used.

sentences.zh: 四年定，先祭六日，百官沐浴宿官署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was fixed: six days before the sacrifice, all officials bathed and lodged in their yamens.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year it was fixed: six days before the sacrifice, all officials bathed and lodged in their yamens.

sentences.zh: 翼日，朝服詣奉天殿丹墀，受誓戒。

translations.literal: The next day, in court dress they proceeded to the red steps of the Hall of Imperial Supremacy and received the oath of abstinence.
