translations.idiomatic: The next day, in court dress they proceeded to the red steps of the Hall of Imperial Supremacy and received the oath of abstinence.

sentences.zh: 丞相以祀期遍告百神，後詣各祠廟行香三日。

translations.literal: The chief minister, on the sacrificial date, announced it throughout to the hundred spirits; afterward he proceeded to each shrine and temple to offer incense for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister announced the sacrificial date throughout to the hundred spirits; afterward he proceeded to each shrine and temple to offer incense for three days.

sentences.zh: 次日，駕詣仁祖廟，告請配享。

translations.literal: The next day, the imperial carriage proceeded to Founder Renzu's temple to announce and request joint enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the imperial carriage proceeded to Founder Renzu's temple to announce and request joint enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，還齋宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he returned to the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he returned to the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 七年，去中嚴、外辦及贊唱上香之縟節，定十二拜禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the cumbersome observances of mid-strictness, outer readiness, and intoned incense offering were removed, and the twelve-bow ritual was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the cumbersome observances of mid-strictness, outer readiness, and intoned incense offering were removed, and the twelve-bow ritual was fixed.

sentences.zh: 十年，改合祀之制，奠玉帛、進俎、三獻，俱先詣上帝神位前，次皇地祇，次仁祖，餘悉仍舊儀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the system of joint sacrifice was changed: presenting jade and silks, advancing the trays, and the three offerings all first proceeded before the Sovereign on High's spirit seat, then the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth, then Founder Renzu; the rest all followed the former ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the system of joint sacrifice was changed: presenting jade and silks, advancing the trays, and the three offerings all first proceeded before the Sovereign on High's spirit seat, then the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth, then Founder Renzu; the rest followed the former ritual.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，罷各廟焚香禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing, the incense-offering rites at the various temples were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 the incense-offering rites at the various temples were abolished.

sentences.zh: 九年，復分祀之制，禮部上大祀圓丘儀註：前期十日，太常寺題請視牲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the system of separate sacrifices was restored; the Ministry of Rites submitted regulations for the great sacrifice at the Circular Mound: ten days beforehand, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized requesting inspection of the victims.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the system of separate sacrifices was restored; the Ministry of Rites submitted regulations for the great sacrifice at the Circular Mound: ten days beforehand, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized requesting inspection of the victims.

sentences.zh: 次請命大臣三員看牲，四員分獻。

translations.literal: Next they requested that three grand ministers inspect the victims and four ministers perform distributed offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Next they requested that three grand ministers inspect the victims and four ministers perform distributed offerings.

sentences.zh: 前期五日，錦衣衛備隨朝駕，帝詣犧牲所視牲。

translations.literal: Five days beforehand, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prepared the escort for the imperial progress; the Emperor proceeded to the victim pens to inspect the victims.
translations.idiomatic: Five days beforehand, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prepared the escort for the imperial progress; the Emperor proceeded to the victim pens to inspect the victims.

sentences.zh: 其前一日，常服告於廟。

translations.literal: The day before, in ordinary dress he announced at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, in ordinary dress he announced at the temple.

sentences.zh: 前期四日，禦奉天殿，太常寺進銅人如常儀。

translations.literal: Four days beforehand, he proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented the bronze figure according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Four days beforehand, he proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented the bronze figure according to the usual ritual.

sentences.zh: 太常博士請太祖祝版於文華殿，候帝親填御名捧出。

translations.literal: A doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested the Grand Ancestor's prayer tablet from the Wenhua Hall, awaiting the Emperor's personally filling in the imperial name and bearing it out.
translations.idiomatic: A doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested the Grand Ancestor's prayer tablet from the Wenhua Hall, awaiting the Emperor's personally filling in the imperial name and bearing it out.

sentences.zh: 前期三日，帝具祭服，以脯醢酒果詣太廟，請太祖配。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand, the Emperor donned sacrificial robes, and with dried meat, sauces, wine, and fruit proceeded to the Grand Temple to request the Grand Ancestor as match.
translations.idiomatic: Three days beforehand, the Emperor donned sacrificial robes and, with dried meat, sauces, wine, and fruit, proceeded to the Grand Temple to request the Grand Ancestor as match.

sentences.zh: 帝還易服，禦奉天殿，百官朝服受誓戒。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned, changed robes, proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, and all officials in court dress received the oath of abstinence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor returned, changed robes, proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, and all officials in court dress received the oath of abstinence.

sentences.zh: 前期二日，太常光祿卿奏省牲，帝至奉天殿親填祝版。

translations.literal: Two days beforehand, the Ministers of Ceremonies and of the Imperial Household reported inspecting the victims; the Emperor proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy and personally filled in the prayer tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Two days beforehand, the Ministers of Ceremonies and of the Imperial Household reported inspecting the victims; the Emperor proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy and personally filled in the prayer tablet.

sentences.zh: 前期一日免朝，錦衣衛備法駕，設版輿於奉天門。

translations.literal: One day beforehand court was excused; the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prepared the imperial equipage and set out the tablet palanquin at the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: One day beforehand court was excused; the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prepared the imperial equipage and set out the tablet palanquin at the Gate of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 常服告廟，乘輿詣南郊，由西天門入，至昭亨門外降輿。

translations.literal: In ordinary dress he announced at the temple, mounted the palanquin, and proceeded to the southern suburb; entering by the Western Heavenly Gate, he descended from the palanquin outside the Gate of Manifest Blessing.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary dress he announced at the temple, mounted the palanquin, and proceeded to the southern suburb; entering by the Western Heavenly Gate, he descended from the palanquin outside the Gate of Manifest Blessing.

sentences.zh: 禮部太常官導由左門入，至內壝。

translations.literal: Officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices guided him in by the left gate to the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices guided him in by the left gate to the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 太常卿導至圜丘，恭視壇位，次至神庫視籩豆，至神廚視牲畢，仍由左門出，升輿，至齋宮。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies guided him to the Circular Mound and reverently inspected the altar site; next to the spirit storehouse to inspect the platters and beans; to the spirit kitchen to inspect the victims; when complete, still by the left gate he went out, mounted the palanquin, and reached the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies guided him to the Circular Mound and reverently inspected the altar site; next to the spirit storehouse to inspect the platters and beans; then to the spirit kitchen to inspect the victims; when complete, he went out by the left gate, mounted the palanquin, and reached the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 分獻陪祀官叩首，禮部太常官詣皇穹宇，請皇天上帝神版、太祖神主、從祀神牌，奉安壇座。

translations.literal: The distributed-offering and attendant-sacrifice officials kowtowed; officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proceeded to the August Vault Shrine, requested the spirit tablets of August Heaven, Sovereign on High, the Grand Ancestor's spirit seat, and the attendant-sacrifice spirit placards, and reverently installed them on the altar seats.
translations.idiomatic: The distributed-offering and attendant-sacrifice officials kowtowed; officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proceeded to the August Vault Shrine, requested the spirit tablets of August Heaven, Sovereign on High, the Grand Ancestor's spirit seat, and the attendant-sacrifice spirit placards, and reverently installed them on the altar seats.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，三鼓，帝自齋宮乘輿至外壝神路之西，降輿至神路東大次。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, at the third drumbeat the Emperor mounted the palanquin from the fasting palace to the west of the spirit road in the outer enclosure, descended from the palanquin, and reached the great tent east of the spirit road.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice, at the third drumbeat the Emperor mounted the palanquin from the fasting palace to the west of the spirit road in the outer enclosure, descended, and reached the great tent east of the spirit road.

sentences.zh: 禮部、太常寺捧神位官復命訖，退。

translations.literal: The officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices who bore the spirit seats reported completion and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices who bore the spirit seats reported completion and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 百官分列神路東西以候。

translations.literal: All officials lined up east and west along the spirit road to await.
translations.idiomatic: All officials lined up east and west along the spirit road to await.

sentences.zh: 帝具祭服出，導引官導由左靈星門入內。

translations.literal: The Emperor donned sacrificial robes and came forth; guiding officers led him in by the left Gate of the Spirit Star.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor donned sacrificial robes and came forth; guiding officers led him in by the left Gate of the Spirit Star.

sentences.zh: 贊對引官導行至內壝，典儀唱樂舞生就位，執事官各司其事。

translations.literal: The intoning and guiding officers led the procession to the inner enclosure; the master of ceremonies chanted that the music and dance performers take their places, and the attendant officers each performed his duty.
translations.idiomatic: The intoning and guiding officers led the procession to the inner enclosure; the master of ceremonies chanted that the music and dance performers take their places, and the attendant officers each performed his duty.

sentences.zh: 帝至禦拜位，自燔柴、迎神至禮畢，其儀悉如舊。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached the imperial bowing place; from burning firewood and welcoming the spirits until the rite was complete, the ritual was entirely as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reached the imperial bowing place; from burning firewood and welcoming the spirits until the rite was complete, the ritual was entirely as before.

sentences.zh: 至大次易服，禮部太常官奉神位安於皇穹宇。

translations.literal: Reaching the great tent he changed robes; officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices bore the spirit seats and installed them in the August Vault Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the great tent he changed robes; officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices bore the spirit seats and installed them in the August Vault Shrine.

sentences.zh: 還齋宮，少憩。

translations.literal: He returned to the fasting palace and rested briefly.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the fasting palace and rested briefly.

sentences.zh: 駕還，詣廟參拜畢。

translations.literal: The imperial progress returned; he proceeded to the temple to pay respects, and when complete,
translations.idiomatic: The imperial progress returned; he proceeded to the temple to pay respects, and when complete,

sentences.zh: 回宮。

translations.literal: He returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔如擬。

translations.literal: An edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 明年，定方澤儀：先期一日，太常卿請太祖配位，奉安皇祇室。

translations.literal: The next year, regulations for the Square Mound sacrifice were fixed: one day beforehand, the Minister of Ceremonies requested the Grand Ancestor's matching seat and reverently installed it in the Chamber of the Imperial Earth Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, regulations for the Square Mound sacrifice were fixed: one day beforehand, the Minister of Ceremonies requested the Grand Ancestor's matching seat and reverently installed it in the Chamber of the Imperial Earth Spirit.

sentences.zh: 至期，禮部太常官同請皇地祇神版、太祖神主、從祀神牌，奉安壇座。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices together requested the spirit tablet of the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth, the Grand Ancestor's spirit seat, and the attendant-sacrifice spirit placards, and reverently installed them on the altar seats.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, officials of the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices together requested the spirit tablet of the Imperial Sovereign Spirit of Earth, the Grand Ancestor's spirit seat, and the attendant-sacrifice spirit placards, and reverently installed them on the altar seats.

sentences.zh: 祀畢，太常奉神版、神牌安皇祇室，奉神主還廟寢。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was complete, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices bore the spirit tablets and placards back to the Chamber of the Imperial Earth Spirit and bore the spirit seat back to the temple dormitory.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was complete, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices bore the spirit tablets and placards back to the Chamber of the Imperial Earth Spirit and bore the spirit seat back to the temple dormitory.

sentences.zh: 餘皆如圜丘儀。

translations.literal: The rest all followed the Circular Mound ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The rest all followed the Circular Mound ritual.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，帝將郊祀，諭禮部尚書夏言欲親行奉安禮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, as the Emperor was about to perform the suburban sacrifice, he instructed Minister of Rites Xia Yan that he wished personally to perform the reverent installation rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, as the Emperor was about to perform the suburban sacrifice, he instructed Minister of Rites Xia Yan that he wished personally to perform the reverent installation rite.

sentences.zh: 言乃擬儀注以聞：先期擇捧主執事官十一員，分獻配殿大臣二員，撰祝文，備脯醢、酒果、制帛、香燭。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon drafted regulations and reported: beforehand select eleven attendant officers to bear the spirit seats, two grand ministers for distributed offerings at the side halls, compose the prayer text, and prepare dried meat, sauces, wine, fruit, prescribed silks, incense, and candles.
translations.idiomatic: Yan thereupon drafted regulations and reported: beforehand select eleven attendant officers to bear the spirit seats, two grand ministers for distributed offerings at the side halls, compose the prayer text, and prepare dried meat, sauces, wine, fruit, prescribed silks, incense, and candles.

sentences.zh: 前一日行告廟禮，設神輿香案於奉天殿，神案二於泰神殿，神案二於東西配殿，香案一于丹墀正中，設大次於圜丘左門外。

translations.literal: The day before, perform the temple-announcement rite; set out the spirit palanquin and incense table in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, two spirit tables in the Great Sacrifice Hall, two spirit tables in the eastern and western side halls, one incense table in the center of the red steps, and set the great tent outside the left gate of the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, perform the temple-announcement rite; set out the spirit palanquin and incense table in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, two spirit tables in the Great Sacrifice Hall, two spirit tables in the eastern and western side halls, one incense table in the center of the red steps, and set the great tent outside the left gate of the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 是日質明，帝常服詣奉天殿，行一拜三叩頭禮。

translations.literal: That day at dawn, the Emperor in ordinary dress proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy and performed one bow and three kowtows.
translations.idiomatic: That day at dawn, the Emperor in ordinary dress proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Supremacy and performed one bow and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 執事官先後捧昊天上帝、太祖高皇帝及從祀神主，各奉安輿中，至圜丘泰神殿門外。

translations.literal: The attendant officers in succession bore the spirit seats of August Heaven, Sovereign on High, the Grand Ancestor, the August Emperor, and the attendant sacrifices, each reverently installing them in the palanquin, and reached the gate outside the Great Sacrifice Hall at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant officers in succession bore the spirit seats of August Heaven, Sovereign on High, the Grand Ancestor, the August Emperor, and the attendant sacrifices, each reverently installing them in the palanquin, and reached the gate outside the Great Sacrifice Hall at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 帝乘輅至昭亨門，禮官導至泰神殿丹墀。

translations.literal: The Emperor mounted the imperial carriage to the Gate of Manifest Blessing; ritual officers guided him to the red steps of the Great Sacrifice Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mounted the imperial carriage to the Gate of Manifest Blessing; ritual officers guided him to the red steps of the Great Sacrifice Hall.

sentences.zh: 執事官就神輿捧神主升石座，奉安於龕中。

translations.literal: The attendant officers took the spirit seats from the palanquin, bore the spirit seats up the stone dais, and reverently installed them in the niches.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant officers took the spirit seats from the palanquin, bore them up the stone dais, and reverently installed them in the niches.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詣香案前，行三獻禮如儀。

translations.literal: The Emperor then proceeded before the incense table and performed the three offerings according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then proceeded before the incense table and performed the three offerings according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，出至大次升座，百官行一拜三叩頭禮畢，還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he went out to the great tent and ascended the seat; when all officials had performed one bow and three kowtows, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he went out to the great tent and ascended the seat; when all officials had performed one bow and three kowtows, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，而命行禮用祭服，導引用太常寺官一員，合禮部堂上官四員。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented, but ordered that sacrificial robes be worn for performing the rite, that one officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices guide, together with four senior officers of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented, but ordered that sacrificial robes be worn for performing the rite, that one officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices guide, together with four senior officers of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬至，尚書言，前此有事南郊，風寒莫備。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of the eleventh year, the minister stated that on the previous occasion of business at the southern suburb, wind and cold had been unprepared for.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of the eleventh year, the minister stated that on the previous occasion of business at the southern suburb, wind and cold had been unprepared for.

sentences.zh: 乃採《禮書》天子祀天張大次、小次之說，請「作黃氈禦幄為小次。

translations.literal: Thereupon adopting from the 《Book of Rites》 the account that when the Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven he pitches a great tent and a small tent, he requested: "Make a yellow-felt imperial canopy as the small tent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon adopting from the 《Book of Rites》 the account that when the Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven he pitches a great tent and a small tent, he requested: "Make a yellow-felt imperial canopy as the small tent.

sentences.zh: 每大祭，所司以隨。

translations.literal: At every great sacrifice, the responsible office shall bring it along.
translations.idiomatic: At every great sacrifice, the responsible office shall bring it along.

sentences.zh: 值風雪，則設於圜丘下，帝就幄中對越，而陟降奠獻乙太常執事官代之」。

translations.literal: When wind and snow occur, set it up below the Circular Mound; the Emperor shall face the spirits within the canopy, while ascending, descending, and presenting offerings shall all be performed by Court of Imperial Sacrifices attendant officers in his stead."

translations.idiomatic: Because the various ministers repeatedly petitioned, permission was granted to perform the Prayer for Grain at the Grand Sacrifice Hall, offering the two founding ancestors as match.

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, the Prayer for Grain rite at the Grand Sacrifice Hall was first performed on the upper xin day of the first month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 the Prayer for Grain rite at the Grand Sacrifice Hall was first performed on the upper xin day of the first month of spring.

translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the Emperor still felt it improper; he instructed Zhang Cong: "From antiquity only an ancestor has been matched with Heaven; now the two founding ancestors are jointly matched—this absolutely must not be taken as a model for later ages.

translations.idiomatic: Silks were reduced by one in ten; the attendant altar was not set up; firewood was not burned—this was fixed as the standard form.

sentences.zh: 十一年驚蟄節，帝疾，不能親，乃命武定侯郭勳代。

translations.idiomatic: At the Awakening of Insects festival of the eleventh year, the Emperor was ill and could not attend in person; he therefore ordered Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun to substitute.

translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, it was changed to be performed in the Mysterious Ultimate Treasure Hall within the inner palace, without offering a match, and this became the fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，禮臣言：「先農親祭，遂耕耤田，即祈穀遺意。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, ritual officials stated: "The personal sacrifice to the First Farmer, followed by plowing the sacred field, preserves the legacy intent of the Prayer for Grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 ritual officials stated: "The personal sacrifice to the First Farmer, followed by plowing the sacred field, preserves the legacy intent of the Prayer for Grain.

translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Mysterious Ultimate Treasure Hall is in the forbidden precinct; for all officials to attend in sacrifice, coming and going is inconvenient.

sentences.zh: ○大雩

translations.literal: ○ Great Rain Prayer
translations.idiomatic: Great Rain Prayer

sentences.zh: 明初，凡水旱災傷及非常變異，或躬禱，或露告於宮中，或於奉天殿陛，或遣官祭告郊廟、陵寢及社稷、山川，無常儀。

translations.literal: In the early Ming, for flood, drought, disaster injury, and unusual anomalies, sometimes the emperor prayed in person, sometimes announced openly in the palace, sometimes at the steps of the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, or dispatched officials to sacrifice and announce at suburban altars and temples, imperial tombs, and the altars of soil and grain and mountains and rivers—there was no fixed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, for flood, drought, disaster injury, and unusual anomalies, sometimes the emperor prayed in person, sometimes announced openly in the palace, sometimes at the steps of the Hall of Imperial Supremacy, or dispatched officials to sacrifice and announce at suburban altars and temples, imperial tombs, and the altars of soil and grain and mountains and rivers—there was no fixed ritual.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，春祈雨，冬祈雪，皆御製祝文，躬祀南郊及山川壇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing, spring prayer for rain and winter prayer for snow were both with imperially composed prayer texts; he personally sacrificed at the southern suburb and the mountains-and-rivers altar.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8, spring prayer for rain and winter prayer for snow were both with imperially composed prayer texts; he personally sacrificed at the southern suburb and the mountains-and-rivers altar.

sentences.zh: 次日，祀社稷壇。

translations.literal: The next day, he sacrificed at the altar of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, he sacrificed at the altar of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 冠服淺色，鹵簿不陳，馳道不除，皆不設配，不奏樂。

translations.literal: Caps and robes were light-colored; the imperial escort array was not displayed; the imperial roadway was not cleared; no match was set up anywhere; music was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Caps and robes were light-colored; the imperial escort array was not displayed; the imperial roadway was not cleared; no match was set up anywhere; music was not performed.

sentences.zh: 九年，帝欲於奉天殿丹陛上行大雩禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Emperor wished to perform the Great Rain Prayer rite on the red steps of the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the Emperor wished to perform the Great Rain Prayer rite on the red steps of the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 夏言言：「按《左傳》『龍見而雩』。

translations.literal: Xia Yan stated: "According to the 《Zuo Commentary》, 'When the dragon appears, perform the rain prayer.'
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan stated: "According to the 《Zuo Commentary》, 'When the dragon appears, perform the rain prayer.'

sentences.zh: 蓋巳月萬物始盛，待雨而大，故祭天為百穀祈膏雨也。

translations.literal: This is because in the si month the myriad things first flourish, awaiting rain to grow great—therefore one sacrifices to Heaven to pray for enriching rain for the hundred grains.
translations.idiomatic: This is because in the si month the myriad things first flourish, awaiting rain to grow great—therefore one sacrifices to Heaven to pray for enriching rain for the hundred grains.

sentences.zh: 《月令》：『雩帝用盛樂，乃命百縣雩祀，祀百辟卿士有益於民者，以祈穀實。

translations.literal: The 《Monthly Ordinances》 says: 'For the rain prayer to the Emperor use magnificent music, and command the hundred districts to perform rain sacrifices, sacrificing to the hundred nobles and officers who benefit the people, to pray for grain abundance.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Monthly Ordinances》 says: 'For the rain prayer to the Emperor use magnificent music, and command the hundred districts to perform rain sacrifices, sacrificing to the hundred nobles and officers who benefit the people, to pray for grain abundance.'

sentences.zh: 』《通典》曰：『巳月雩五方上帝，其壇名雩，禜於南郊之傍。

translations.literal: ' The 《Comprehensive Institutions》 states: 'In the si month sacrifice to the Five Directional Sovereigns on High at the rain prayer; its altar is named the rain altar, with a subsidiary rite beside the southern suburb.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The 《Comprehensive Institutions》 states: 'In the si month sacrifice to the Five Directional Sovereigns on High at the rain prayer; its altar is named the rain altar, with a subsidiary rite beside the southern suburb.'

translations.literal: ' Former minister Qiu Jun also said: 'Apart from suburban sacrifice to Heaven, the Son of Heaven separately establishes an altar to pray for rain.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Former minister Qiu Jun also said: 'Apart from suburban sacrifice to Heaven, the Son of Heaven separately establishes an altar to pray for rain.'

sentences.zh: 後世此禮不傳，遇有旱，輒假異端之人為祈禱之事，不務以誠意感格，而以法術劫制，誣亦甚矣。

translations.literal: ' Later ages did not transmit this rite; when drought calamity occurred, they would resort to heterodox persons to perform prayer services, not seeking to move [Heaven] through sincerity but coercing by occult techniques—the deception is extreme indeed.
translations.idiomatic: ' Later ages did not transmit this rite; when drought calamity occurred, they would resort to heterodox persons to perform prayer services, not seeking to move Heaven through sincerity but coercing by occult techniques—the deception is extreme indeed.

sentences.zh: 』浚意欲於郊傍擇地為雩壇，孟夏後行禮。

translations.literal: ' Jun's intent was to select ground beside the suburb for a rain-prayer altar and perform the rite after mid-summer."
translations.idiomatic: ' Jun's intent was to select ground beside the suburb for a rain-prayer altar and perform the rite after mid-summer."

sentences.zh: 臣以為孟春既祈穀矣，苟自二月至四月，雨暘時若，則大雩之祭，可遣官攝行。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that since in early spring the grain-prayer [rite] has already been performed, if from the second month through the fourth month rain and sunshine are timely, then the Great Rain Prayer sacrifice may have an official dispatched to perform it by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that once the early-spring grain-prayer rite has been performed, if from the second month through the fourth month rain and sunshine are timely, the Great Rain Prayer may be delegated to an acting official.

translations.literal: If rain and moisture miss their season, then Your Majesty should personally perform the prayers.
translations.idiomatic: If rain and moisture miss their season, Your Majesty should perform the prayers in person.

translations.idiomatic: " The court then built the Lofty Rain Prayer altar east of the Taiyuan Gate outside the Round Mound altar, one tier in design; in drought years they prayed there, with Taizu as match.

sentences.zh: 十二年，夏言等言：「古者大雩之祀，命樂正習盛樂、舞皇舞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Xia Yan and others stated: "In antiquity at the Great Rain Prayer sacrifice, they ordered the Director of Music to rehearse magnificent music and dance the August Dance.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 12, Xia Yan and others stated: "In antiquity the Great Rain Prayer sacrifice ordered the Director of Music to rehearse magnificent music and perform the August Dance.

sentences.zh: 蓋假聲容之和，以宣陰陽之氣。

translations.literal: This was to borrow the harmony of sound and appearance to express the qi of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: This was to borrow the harmony of sound and spectacle to give expression to the qi of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 請於三獻禮成之後，九奏樂止之時，樂奏《雲門之舞》。

translations.literal: We request that after the three offerings are complete and when the nine performances of music cease, music perform the 《Cloud Gate Dance》.
translations.idiomatic: We request that after the three offerings are complete and the nine musical performances have ended, the 《Cloud Gate Dance》 be performed.

sentences.zh: 仍命儒臣括《雲漢》詩詞，制《雲門》一曲，使文武舞士並舞而歌之。

translations.literal: Also command Confucian officials to compile words from the 《Clouds Wide》 ode and compose one piece 《Cloud Gate》, causing civil and martial dancers together to dance and sing it.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that Confucian officials compile verses from the 《Clouds Wide》 ode to compose a 《Cloud Gate》 piece, with civil and martial dancers performing and singing it together.

sentences.zh: 蓋《雲門》者，帝堯之樂，《周官》以祀天神，取雲出天氣，雨出地氣也。

translations.literal: For 《Cloud Gate》 is the music of Emperor Yao; the 《Rites of Zhou》 uses it to sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit, taking that clouds issue from Heaven's qi and rain issues from Earth's qi.
translations.idiomatic: For 《Cloud Gate》 is the music of Emperor Yao; the 《Rites of Zhou》 employs it in sacrifice to the Heavenly Spirit, signifying that clouds arise from Heaven's qi and rain from Earth's qi.

sentences.zh: 且請增鼓吹數番，教舞童百人，青衣執羽，繞壇歌《雲門之曲》而舞，曲凡九成。

translations.literal: Moreover they requested increasing several rounds of drum-and-pipe music, instructing a hundred dance youths in blue garments holding plumes, circling the altar singing the 《Cloud Gate》 melody while dancing—the piece has nine sections in all.
translations.idiomatic: They also requested additional rounds of drum-and-pipe music and a hundred dance youths in blue garments bearing plumes to circle the altar, singing the 《Cloud Gate》 melody as they danced—the piece comprising nine sections in all.

translations.idiomatic: " They then submitted the regulations, modeled on the grain-prayer rite.

sentences.zh: 又言：「大雩乃祀天禱雨之祭。

translations.literal: They also stated: "The Great Rain Prayer is the sacrifice of sacrificing to Heaven and praying for rain.
translations.idiomatic: They also stated: "The Great Rain Prayer is the rite of sacrificing to Heaven and praying for rain.

sentences.zh: 凡遇亢旱，則禮部於春末請行之。

translations.literal: Whenever severe drought is encountered, the Ministry of Rites at spring's end requests its performance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever severe drought occurred, the Ministry of Rites would request its performance at the end of spring.

translations.literal: ○ Rites of the Great Feast
translations.idiomatic: Rites of the Great Feast

sentences.zh: 明初無明堂之制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming there were no regulations for the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming there was no Bright Hall institution.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年六月，致仕揚州府同知豐坊上疏言：「孝莫大於嚴父，嚴父莫大於配天。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Jiajing 17, Feng Fang, retired associate prefect of Yangzhou Prefecture, submitted a memorial stating: "Among filial acts none is greater than honoring the father; among honoring the father none is greater than matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jiajing 17, Feng Fang, retired associate prefect of Yangzhou, memorialized: "No filial act exceeds honoring one's father, and no honor to the father exceeds matching him with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請復古禮，建明堂。

translations.literal: We request restoring the ancient rites and building a Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the ancient rites be restored and a Bright Hall built.

sentences.zh: 加尊皇考獻皇帝廟號稱宗，以配上帝。

translations.literal: Add exalted title to the imperial father's temple name, calling him Zong, to match the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Exalt my late imperial father the Xian Emperor with the temple title Zong, to match the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 」下禮部會議。

translations.literal: " It was sent down to the Ministry of Rites for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書嚴嵩等言：

translations.literal: Minister Yan Song and others stated:
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yan Song and others replied:

sentences.zh: 昔羲、農肇祀上帝，或為明堂。

translations.literal: Formerly Fu Xi and Shen Nong first sacrificed to the Supreme Lord, perhaps as the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Fu Xi and Shen Nong first sacrificed to the Supreme Lord, perhaps in what became the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 嗣是夏后氏世室，殷人重屋，周人作明堂之制，視夏、殷加詳焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Xia had the World Chamber, the Yin had the Double Eaves, and the Zhou instituted Bright Hall regulations, more detailed than Xia and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Xia established the World Chamber, the Shang the Double Eaves, and the Zhou the Bright Hall system—more elaborate than what preceded.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖王事天，如子事父，體尊而情親。

translations.literal: For the sage king serves Heaven as a son serves a father—status exalted yet sentiment intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The sage king serves Heaven as a son serves his father—reverent in station yet intimate in feeling.

sentences.zh: 故制為一歲享祀之禮，冬至圜丘，孟春祈穀，孟夏雩壇，季秋明堂，皆所以尊之也。

translations.literal: Therefore they instituted the rites of annual feasting: winter solstice at the Round Mound, early spring grain prayer, early summer rain altar, late autumn Bright Hall—all means of honoring Him.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the annual cycle of feasts: winter solstice at the Round Mound, early spring grain prayer, early summer at the rain altar, late autumn at the Bright Hall—all to honor Heaven.

sentences.zh: 明堂帝而享之，又以親之也。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall one treats Him as Emperor and feasts Him, yet also draws Him near in intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall one feasts Him as Emperor, yet also draws near in intimacy.

sentences.zh: 今日創制，古法難尋，要在師先王之意。

translations.literal: Today in establishing institutions, ancient methods are hard to find; the essential lies in taking the former kings' intent as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing institutions today, ancient methods are hard to recover; what matters is to follow the intent of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 明堂圜丘，皆所以事天，今大祀殿在圜丘之北，禁城東西，正應古之方位。

translations.literal: Bright Hall and Round Mound are both means of serving Heaven; now the Great Sacrifice Hall is north of the Round Mound, east and west within the Forbidden City—exactly matching the ancient orientations.
translations.idiomatic: Both Bright Hall and Round Mound serve Heaven; the Great Sacrifice Hall now stands north of the Round Mound, east and west within the Forbidden City—precisely matching the ancient orientations.

sentences.zh: 明堂秋享，即以大祀殿行之為當。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall autumn feast, performed at the Great Sacrifice Hall, is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall autumn feast should properly be performed at the Great Sacrifice Hall.

sentences.zh: 至配侑之禮，昔周公宗祀文王於明堂，詩傳以為物成形於帝，猶人成形於父。

translations.literal: As for the rite of matched accompaniment, formerly the Duke of Zhou made lineage sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall; the Poetry tradition holds that things take form from the Emperor as humans take form from the father.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rite of matched accompaniment, the Duke of Zhou once performed lineage sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall; the Poetry commentators hold that things take form from the Emperor as a person takes form from the father.

sentences.zh: 故季秋祀帝明堂，而以父配之，取其物之時也。

translations.literal: Therefore in late autumn one sacrifices to the Emperor at the Bright Hall and matches the father—taking the season when things [reach maturity].
translations.idiomatic: Hence in late autumn one sacrifices to the Emperor at the Bright Hall and matches one's father—taking the season when things reach maturity.

sentences.zh: 漢孝武明堂之享，以景帝配，孝章以光武配，唐中宗以高宗配，明皇以睿宗配，代宗以肅宗配，宋真宗乙太宗配，仁宗以真宗配，英宗以仁宗配，皆世以遞配，此主於親親也。

translations.literal: Han Emperor Wu's Bright Hall feast matched Emperor Jing; Emperor Zhang matched Guangwu; Tang Zhongzong matched Gaozong; Ming Huang matched Ruizong; Daizong matched Suzong; Song Zhenzong matched Taizong; Emperor Renzong matched Zhenzong; Yingzong matched Renzong—all generations in succession matching; this emphasizes kinship among kin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han matched Emperor Jing at the Bright Hall feast; Emperor Zhang matched Guangwu; Tang Zhongzong matched Gaozong; Emperor Xuanzong matched Ruizong; Daizong matched Suzong; Song Zhenzong matched Taizong; Renzong matched Zhenzong; Yingzong matched Renzong—each generation matching in turn. This tradition emphasizes kinship among kin.

sentences.zh: 宋錢公輔曰：「郊之祭，以始封之祖，有聖人之功者配焉。

translations.literal: Song official Qian Gongfu said: "At the suburban sacrifice, match the ancestor of the first enfeoffment who has the merit of a sage.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gongfu of Song said: "At the suburban sacrifice, one matches the founding ancestor who possesses a sage's merit.

sentences.zh: 明堂之祭，以繼體之君，有聖人之德者配焉。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall sacrifice, match the ruler who succeeded to the line who has the virtue of a sage.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall sacrifice, one matches the ruler who succeeded to the throne and possesses a sage's virtue.

sentences.zh: 」當時司馬光、孫抃諸臣執辨於朝，程、硃大賢倡議於下，此主於祖宗之功德也。

translations.literal: " At that time Sima Guang, Sun Bian, and other ministers argued in court; the great worthies Cheng and Zhu advocated below—this emphasizes the merit and virtue of ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Sima Guang, Sun Bian, and others debated in court, while the great worthies Cheng and Zhu championed the view from below—this tradition emphasizes the merit and virtue of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今復古明堂大享之制，其所當配之帝，亦惟二說而已。

translations.literal: Now in restoring the ancient Bright Hall Great Feast institution, the Supreme Lord who ought to be matched has only these two positions.
translations.idiomatic: In restoring the ancient Bright Hall Great Feast, only these two views exist as to who should be matched with the Lord.

sentences.zh: 若以功德論，則太宗再造家邦，功符太祖，當配乙太宗。

translations.literal: If judged by merit and virtue, Taizong twice rebuilt the realm, his merit matching Taizu—ought to match Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: If judged by merit and virtue, Taizong twice restored the realm and his achievement equals Taizu's—he ought to be matched.

sentences.zh: 若以親親論，則獻皇帝陛下之所自出，陛下之功德，即皇考之功德，當配以獻皇帝。

translations.literal: If judged by kinship among kin, the Xian Emperor is Your Majesty's source; Your Majesty's merit and virtue are the late emperor father's merit and virtue—ought to match the Xian Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: If judged by kinship, the Xian Emperor is Your Majesty's progenitor; Your Majesty's merit and virtue are your late father's merit and virtue—the Xian Emperor ought to be matched.

sentences.zh: 至稱宗之說，則臣等不敢妄議。

translations.literal: As for the proposal to call him Zong, your subjects dare not presume to discuss rashly.
translations.idiomatic: As for the proposal to confer the title Zong, your subjects dare not venture an opinion.

sentences.zh: 帝降旨：「明堂秋報大禮，於奉天殿行，其配帝務求畫一之說。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued a rescript: "The great rite of the Bright Hall autumn harvest report shall be performed at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy; on matching the Lord seek one unified position.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a rescript: "The great Bright Hall autumn harvest rite shall be performed at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy; on who shall be matched with the Lord, seek a single unified view.

sentences.zh: 皇考稱宗，何為不可？

translations.literal: Calling the imperial father Zong—why may it not be done?
translations.idiomatic: Why may my late imperial father not be called Zong?

sentences.zh: 再會議以聞。

translations.literal: Deliberate again and report.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate again and report back.

sentences.zh: 」於是戶部左侍郎唐胄抗疏言：

translations.literal: " Thereupon Left Vice Minister of Revenue Tang Zhou submitted a resisting memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Tang Zhou, left vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, submitted a dissenting memorial:

sentences.zh: 三代之禮，莫備於周。

translations.literal: Of the Three Dynasties' rites, none is more complete than Zhou's.
translations.idiomatic: Of the ritual systems of the Three Dynasties, none surpasses that of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》曰：「郊祀后稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝。

translations.literal: The 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: "Suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji to match Heaven; lineage sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to match the Supreme Lord."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: "At the suburban sacrifice Hou Ji is matched with Heaven; at lineage sacrifice King Wen is honored in the Bright Hall and matched with the Supreme Lord."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「嚴父莫大於配天，則周公其人也。

translations.literal: It also says: "Among honoring the father none is greater than matching Heaven—then the Duke of Zhou is the man."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Nothing in honoring one's father exceeds matching him with Heaven—and the Duke of Zhou was such a man."

sentences.zh: 」說者謂周公有聖人之德，製作禮樂，而文王適其父，故引以證聖人之孝，答曾子問而已。

translations.literal: " Expositors say the Duke of Zhou had the virtue of a sage and made rites and music, while King Wen happened to be his father—therefore [the passage] cites this to prove a sage's filial piety, merely answering Zengzi's question.
translations.idiomatic: " Commentators hold that the Duke of Zhou possessed a sage's virtue and fashioned rites and music, while King Wen happened to be his father—the passage cites this only to illustrate a sage's filial piety in answer to Zengzi's question.

sentences.zh: 非謂有天下者皆必以父配天，然後為孝。

translations.literal: It does not mean that all who possess the realm must match their father to Heaven before they are filial.
translations.idiomatic: It does not mean that every ruler must match his father with Heaven in order to be filial.

sentences.zh: 不然，周公輔成王踐阼，其禮蓋為成王而制，於周公為嚴父，於成王則為嚴祖矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng in ascending the throne; its rites were largely made for King Cheng—in the Duke of Zhou's case a stern father, in King Cheng's case a stern ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise: the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng to the throne, and those rites were largely fashioned for King Cheng—for the Duke of Zhou they concerned honoring a father, but for King Cheng they concerned honoring an ancestor.

sentences.zh: 然周公歸政之後，未聞成王以嚴父之故，廢文王配天之祭，而移於武王也。

translations.literal: Yet after the Duke of Zhou returned power, one does not hear that King Cheng, because of honoring his father, abolished King Wen's sacrifice matched to Heaven and transferred it to King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after the Duke of Zhou returned power, we never hear that King Cheng, out of filial regard for his father, abolished King Wen's matching sacrifice to Heaven and transferred it to King Wu.

sentences.zh: 後世祀明堂者，皆配以父，此乃誤《孝經》之義，而違先王之禮。

translations.literal: Later ages sacrificing at the Bright Hall all matched the father—this misreads the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and violates the former kings' rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages, in sacrificing at the Bright Hall, all matched the reigning ruler's father—misreading the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and violating the rites of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 昔有問於硃熹曰：「周公之後，當以文王配耶，當以時王之父配耶？

translations.literal: Formerly someone asked Zhu Xi: "After the Duke of Zhou, should King Wen be matched, or the reigning king's father matched?
translations.idiomatic: Someone once asked Zhu Xi: "After the Duke of Zhou, should King Wen be matched, or the reigning king's father?

sentences.zh: 」熹曰：「只當以文王為配。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "One should only match King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi replied: "Only King Wen should be matched.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「繼周者如何？

translations.literal: " He was also asked: "What of those succeeding Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: " He was asked further: "What of those who succeeded Zhou?

sentences.zh: 」熹曰：「只以有功之祖配，後來第為嚴父說所惑亂耳。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Only match the ancestor of merit; later people were merely confused by the doctrine of honoring the father."
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said: "Match only the meritorious ancestor; later generations were simply misled by the doctrine of honoring the father."

sentences.zh: 」由此觀之，明堂之配，不專於父明矣。

translations.literal: " From this perspective, Bright Hall matching is not exclusively the father—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: " From this it is clear that Bright Hall matching is not exclusively the father.

sentences.zh: 今禮臣不能辨嚴父之非，不舉文、武、成、康之盛，而乃濫引漢、唐、宋不足法之事為言，謂之何哉！

translations.literal: Now the ritual ministers cannot distinguish the error of honoring the father, do not cite the glory of Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, yet indiscriminately cite Han, Tang, and Song precedents unworthy of emulation—what is one to call this!
translations.idiomatic: Today the ritual officials cannot discern the error in the doctrine of honoring the father, cite not the splendor of the Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang reigns, yet indiscriminately invoke Han, Tang, and Song precedents unworthy of emulation—what shall one call this!

sentences.zh: 雖然，豐坊明堂之議，雖未可從，而明堂之禮，則不可廢。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, though Feng Fang's Bright Hall proposal cannot yet be followed, the Bright Hall rite cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, though Feng Fang's Bright Hall proposal cannot yet be adopted, the Bright Hall rite itself must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今南、北兩郊皆主尊尊，必季秋一大享帝，而親親之義始備。

translations.literal: Now both southern and northern suburbs emphasize exalted respect; only with one great autumn feast to the Emperor does the meaning of kinship intimacy become complete.
translations.idiomatic: Today both southern and northern suburban sacrifices emphasize supreme reverence; only with a great autumn feast to the Emperor is the principle of intimate kinship fully realized.

sentences.zh: 自三代以來，郊與明堂各立所配之帝。

translations.literal: Since the Three Dynasties, suburban sacrifice and Bright Hall each established their own matched Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Dynasties, suburban sacrifice and Bright Hall each had their own matched Lord.

sentences.zh: 太祖、大宗功德並盛，比之於周，太祖則后稷也，太宗則文王也。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong's merit and virtue both flourished; compared to Zhou, Taizu is Hou Ji and Taizong is King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Taizong alike possessed outstanding merit and virtue; compared with Zhou, Taizu corresponds to Hou Ji and Taizong to King Wen.

sentences.zh: 今兩郊及祈穀，皆奉配太祖，而太宗獨未有配。

translations.literal: Now both suburbs and grain prayer all present Taizu as match, while Taizong alone has no match.
translations.idiomatic: Today both suburban sacrifices and the grain prayer present Taizu as match, yet Taizong alone has none.

sentences.zh: 甚為缺典。

translations.literal: This is a grave lacuna in the canon.
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave defect in our ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 故今奉天殿大享之祭，必奉配太宗，而後我朝之典禮始備。

translations.literal: Therefore today's Great Feast sacrifice at the Hall of Imperial Supremacy must present Taizong as match, and only then will our dynasty's canonical rites be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at today's Great Feast in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy Taizong must be presented as match—only then will our dynasty's canonical rites be complete.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下胄詔獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and sent Zhou to imperial prison by edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and had Zhou imprisoned by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 嵩乃再會廷臣，先議配帝之禮，言：「考季秋成物之指，嚴父配天之文，宜奉獻皇帝配帝侑食。

translations.literal: Song then again convoked court ministers, first deliberating the rite of matching the Lord, stating: "Considering the purport of late autumn when things are ripe and the text on honoring the father by matching Heaven, the Xian Emperor ought to be presented matching the Lord to assist the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Song then reconvened the court ministers to deliberate first the rite of matching the Lord, stating: "Considering the meaning of late autumn when things ripen, and the passage on honoring the father by matching Heaven, the Xian Emperor ought to be presented to match the Lord and assist at the feast.

sentences.zh: 」因請奉文皇帝配祀於孟春祈穀。

translations.literal: " He therefore requested presenting the Wen Emperor as match at early-spring grain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: " He also requested that the Wen Emperor be presented as match at the early-spring grain prayer.

sentences.zh: 帝從獻皇配帝之請，而卻文皇議不行。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed the request to match the Xian Emperor to the Lord but rejected the Wen Emperor proposal, which was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted the request to match the Xian Emperor with the Lord but rejected the proposal regarding the Wen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 已復以稱宗之禮，集文武大臣於東閣議，言：「《禮》稱：『祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: Then again regarding the rite of calling Zong, he gathered civil and military great ministers at the Eastern Pavilion to deliberate, stating: "The 《Rites》 says: 'Zu is for merit, Zong is for virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: He then convened civil and military ministers at the Eastern Pavilion to deliberate the conferral of the title Zong, stating: "The 《Rites》 says: 'Zu honors merit; Zong honors virtue.'

sentences.zh: 』釋者曰：『祖，始也。

translations.literal: ' Expositors say: 'Zu means beginning.
translations.idiomatic: ' Commentators explain: 'Zu means beginning.

sentences.zh: 宗，尊也。

translations.literal: Zong means honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zong means honor.

sentences.zh: 』《漢書注》曰：『祖之稱始，始受命也。

translations.literal: ' The 《Book of Han》 commentary says: 'The title zu means beginning—beginning to receive the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: ' The commentary on the 《Book of Han》 says: 'The title zu means beginning—beginning to receive the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 宗之稱尊，有德可尊也。

translations.literal: The title zong means honor—having virtue worthy of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The title zong means honor—having virtue worthy of honor.

sentences.zh: 』《孝經》曰：『宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: ' The 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: 'Lineage sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall to match the Supreme Lord.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The 《Classic of Filial Piety》 says: 'Perform lineage sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall to match the Supreme Lord.'

sentences.zh: 』王肅注曰：『周公於文王，尊而祀之也。

translations.literal: ' Wang Su's commentary says: 'The Duke of Zhou toward King Wen honored and sacrificed to him.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Wang Su's commentary says: 'The Duke of Zhou honored King Wen and sacrificed to him.'

sentences.zh: 』此宗尊之說也。

translations.literal: ' This is the doctrine of zong as honor.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is the doctrine that zong signifies honor.

sentences.zh: 古者天子七廟。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven had seven ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven maintained seven ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 劉歆曰：「七者正法，苟有功德則宗之，不可預為設數。

translations.literal: Liu Xin said: "Seven is the correct standard; when there is merit or virtue one honors as zong—one cannot preset the number in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin said: "Seven is the correct norm; when merit or virtue warrants it one honors a forebear as zong—the number cannot be fixed in advance.

sentences.zh: 宗不在數中，宗變也。

translations.literal: Zong is not counted in the number; zong is exceptional."
translations.idiomatic: Zong is not counted in the number; zong is an exceptional honor."

sentences.zh: 』硃熹亦以歆之說為然。

translations.literal: ' Zhu Xi also held Xin's doctrine correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi likewise accepted Xin's view.

sentences.zh: 陳氏《禮書》曰：『父昭子穆，而有常數者，禮也。

translations.literal: Master Chen's 《Book of Rites》 says: 'Father bright and son reverent, with a fixed number—this is ritual norm.
translations.idiomatic: Master Chen's 《Book of Rites》 says: 'Father in the bright position and son in the reverent position, with a fixed number—this is ritual norm.

sentences.zh: 祖功宗德，而無定法者，義也。

translations.literal: Merit for zu and virtue for zong without fixed law—this is principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zu for merit and zong for virtue without fixed rule—this is principle.

sentences.zh: 』此宗無數之說，禮以義起者。

translations.literal: ' This is the doctrine that zong has no fixed number—rites arise from principle.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is the doctrine that zong has no fixed number—rites arise from principle.

sentences.zh: 今援據古義，推緣人情，皇考至德昭聞，密佑穹旻，宗以其德可。

translations.literal: Now citing ancient principle and extending human sentiment, the imperial father's supreme virtue is renowned, secretly aiding the azure heavens—zong by his virtue is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Citing ancient principle and extending human sentiment, the late imperial father's supreme virtue is renowned and he secretly aids the azure heavens—he may be honored as zong by virtue.

sentences.zh: 聖子神孫，傳授無疆，皆皇考一人所衍布，宗以其世亦可。

translations.literal: The sage son and divine grandsons, transmission without bound—all extended and spread by the imperial father alone; zong by his lineage is also permissible.
translations.idiomatic: The sage son and divine grandsons, their succession without end—all extended by the late imperial father alone—he may also be honored as zong by lineage.

sentences.zh: 宜加宗皇考，配帝明堂，永為有德不遷之廟。

translations.literal: One ought to add zong to the imperial father, match the Lord at the Bright Hall, establishing forever a temple of virtue not to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: The late imperial father ought to receive the title Zong, match the Lord at the Bright Hall, and be established forever as a temple of virtue not subject to removal.

sentences.zh: 」帝以疏不言祔廟，留中不下，乃設為臣下奏對之詞，作《明堂或問》，以示輔臣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, because the memorial did not speak of enshrining in the ancestral temple, kept it within and did not issue it; he then fashioned words of ministers' memorial responses, composing 《Questions on the Bright Hall》 to show assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Because the memorial did not address enshrinement in the ancestral temple, the Emperor kept it within and did not promulgate it; he then composed ministerial questions and answers in 《Questions on the Bright Hall》 and showed it to his assisting ministers.

sentences.zh: 大略言：「文皇遠祖，不應嚴父之義，宜以父配。

translations.literal: In summary it stated: "The Wen Emperor is a remote ancestor and does not fit the meaning of honoring the father—one ought to match the father.
translations.idiomatic: In summary it stated: "The Wen Emperor is a remote ancestor and does not satisfy the principle of honoring the father—one ought to match the father.

sentences.zh: 稱宗雖無定說，尊親崇上，義所當行。

translations.literal: Though calling Zong has no fixed doctrine, exalting kin and elevating superiors is righteousness that ought to be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Though the title Zong has no fixed doctrine, exalting kin and elevating superiors is righteousness that ought to be practiced.

sentences.zh: 既稱宗，則當祔廟，豈有太廟中四親不具之禮？

translations.literal: Once called Zong, one ought to enshrine in the temple—how could there be rites in the Grand Temple where the four kin are incomplete?
translations.idiomatic: Once called Zong, one ought to be enshrined in the ancestral temple—how could the Grand Temple rites leave the four kin incomplete?

sentences.zh: 」帝既排正議，崇私親，心念太宗永無配享，無以謝廷臣，乃定獻皇配帝稱宗，而改稱太宗號曰成祖。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, having rejected correct debate and elevated private kin, mindful that Taizong would forever lack matched feast, with no means to answer court ministers, then fixed the Xian Emperor matching the Lord and called Zong, and changed Taizong's title to Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, having rejected orthodox debate and elevated his private kin, mindful that Taizong would forever lack a matched feast and unable to satisfy the court, fixed the Xian Emperor as match with the Lord and called him Zong, and changed Taizong's title to Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 時未建明堂，迫季秋。

translations.literal: At the time the Bright Hall was not yet built, as late autumn pressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall had not yet been built, and late autumn was pressing.

sentences.zh: 遂大享上帝於玄極寶殿，奉睿宗獻皇帝配。

translations.literal: He then performed the Great Feast to the Supreme Lord at the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate Treasure, presenting the Ruizong Xian Emperor as match.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore performed the Great Feast to the Supreme Lord in the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate Treasure, with the Ruizong Xian Emperor as match.

sentences.zh: 殿在宮右乾隅，舊名欽安殿。

translations.literal: The hall was in the qian corner at the palace's right, formerly named the Hall of Reverent Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: The hall stood in the qian corner at the right of the palace, formerly called the Hall of Reverent Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 禮成，禮部請帝升殿，百官表賀，如郊祀慶成儀。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the Ministry of Rites requested the Emperor ascend the hall; all officials submitted felicitations as in the suburban sacrifice celebration rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the Ministry of Rites requested that the Emperor ascend the hall; all officials submitted congratulatory memorials as in the suburban sacrifice celebration rites.

sentences.zh: 帝以大享初舉，命賜宴羣臣於謹身殿。

translations.literal: Because the Great Feast was newly instituted, the Emperor ordered a banquet bestowed on the assembled ministers at the Hall of Self-Discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Great Feast was being held for the first time, the Emperor ordered a banquet for the assembled ministers in the Hall of Self-Discipline.

sentences.zh: 已而以足疾不御殿，命羣臣勿行賀禮。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because of foot ailment he did not ascend the hall and ordered ministers not to perform congratulatory rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because of a foot ailment he did not ascend the hall and ordered the ministers not to perform congratulatory rites.

sentences.zh: 禮官以表聞，並罷宴，令光祿寺分給。

translations.literal: Ritual officials reported by memorial; the banquet was also canceled and the Office of Imperial Commissary ordered to distribute portions.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials reported by memorial; the banquet was also canceled, and the Office of Imperial Commissary was ordered to distribute the provisions.

sentences.zh: ○令節拜天

translations.literal: ○ Statutory Festivals: Worshipping Heaven
translations.idiomatic: Statutory Festivals: Worshipping Heaven

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，沿先朝舊儀，每日宮中行拜天禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, following the old rites of previous reigns, the worship of Heaven was performed daily within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jiajing, following the old rites of previous reigns, the worship of Heaven was performed daily within the palace.

sentences.zh: 後以為瀆，罷之。

translations.literal: Later it was deemed irreverent and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was deemed irreverent and abolished.

sentences.zh: 遇正旦、冬至、聖誕節，於奉天殿丹陛上行禮。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the Emperor's birthday, the ritual was performed on the red steps of the Hall of Receiving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the Emperor's birthday, the ritual was performed on the red steps of the Hall of Receiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 既定郊祀，遂罷冬至之禮。

translations.literal: Once the suburban sacrifice was fixed, the winter solstice ritual was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Once the suburban sacrifice was fixed, the winter solstice ritual was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 惟正旦、聖誕節行禮於玄極寶殿。

translations.literal: Only on New Year's Day and the Emperor's birthday was the ritual performed in the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate Treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Only on New Year's Day and the Emperor's birthday was the ritual performed in the Hall of the Mysterious Ultimate Treasure.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年正旦，命宮中拜天，不用在外執事，祭品亦不取供於太常。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the first year of Longqing, he ordered worship of Heaven within the palace, without using attendants from outside, and sacrificial offerings were no longer supplied by the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Longqing 1 he ordered worship of Heaven within the palace, without using attendants from outside, and sacrificial offerings were no longer supplied by the Ministry of Ceremonies.
